stories.title: Wendy's Sued Over Alleged Nationwide Menu Pricing Coordination
stories.summary:
Fast-food operator Wendy's and software provider NCR Voyix face a proposed class-action lawsuit in the United States. Filed on Monday in a federal court in Maryland by California resident Andy Garcia, the complaint alleges the companies conspired to inflate menu prices across the country by sharing sensitive sales information and centralizing pricing decisions. The lawsuit claims Wendy's acts as a common decisionmaker for independent franchisees and company-owned locations, violating US antitrust law.

According to the legal filing, the alleged coordination scheme began as early as 2016. The plaintiff's attorney, Allen Neumark, stated that Wendy's misleadingly tells investors that individual franchisees establish their own prices. The lawsuit asserts that Wendy's mandates competing franchisees to use NCR's Aloha point-of-sale software to supply detailed transaction data. This information is allegedly used to coordinate prices among restaurants that should otherwise be competitors, ultimately causing consumers to pay higher costs.

This legal action is part of a broader trend of litigation scrutinizing how businesses utilize technology and pricing data. In October, McDonald's faced a similar lawsuit regarding the alleged misuse of AI tools to set menu prices, though McDonald's has denied wrongdoing. The Wendy's lawsuit was filed on behalf of at least tens of thousands of customers and seeks unspecified monetary damages alongside a court order to halt the alleged pricing practices.

Neither Wendy's nor NCR Voyix provided an immediate response to requests for comment regarding the allegations. The case highlights increasing regulatory and legal scrutiny over corporate pricing mechanisms and software networks within the fast-food industry. If successful, the lawsuit could significantly alter how major restaurant chains manage franchise pricing and data-sharing strategies nationwide.

stories.title: Pakistan Invites Maldives Investment After Securing Tuna Quota
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry invited the Maldives to invest in Pakistan's emerging tuna-processing and canning sector. The offer was extended during a meeting in Islamabad with an eight-member Maldivian delegation led by Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Mohamed Ameen. Both nations are working to enhance trade, maritime connectivity, and cooperation within the blue economy.

During the discussions, Junaid Chaudhry announced that Pakistan has secured a tuna quota of 25,000 metric tonnes from the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission for the first time. This allocation consists of 15,000 tonnes of yellowfin tuna and 10,000 tonnes of skipjack. He noted that the quota could potentially generate approximately $200 million in export earnings. The minister emphasized that sustainable fishing practices, international partnerships, and policy reforms can help expand exports, attract foreign investment, and protect marine resources.

In addition to the fisheries sector, the two sides explored potential collaboration in tourism, medical tourism, food security, and medical equipment. They also discussed ways to improve transport links and bilateral trade. A joint working group has been established to identify trade opportunities and develop recommendations ahead of a high-level Pakistani delegation's visit to the Maldives in December to further economic cooperation.

The Maldivian delegation included Deputy Minister of Tourism and Civil Aviation Mohamed Awadh, Maldivian High Commissioner to Pakistan Mohamed Thoha, and senior aviation officials. The engagement underscores both countries' efforts to deepen bilateral ties and leverage new economic opportunities in maritime industries and regional trade.

stories.title: Why Fragmented Farms and Missing Cooperatives Stall Pakistan's Agriculture
stories.summary:
Pakistan's agricultural sector remains small, fragmented, and expensive due to a lack of farmer cooperatives and collective scale. According to the country's first digital agricultural census released in 2025, Pakistan has 11.7 million farms, up from 8.3 million in 2010, while the average farm size has decreased from 6.4 acres to 5.1 acres. Approximately 97 percent of farmers own less than 12.5 acres, and nearly half of all farms are divided into separate pieces that shrink further with each inheritance. Small, scattered plots make mechanization and modern irrigation costly, forcing farmers to buy retail inputs, borrow from local agents at informal rates, and sell independently.

The absence of cooperatives is evident in the dairy sector. Although Pakistan is the world's fourth-largest milk producer with an output exceeding 60 million tonnes annually, about 95 percent of the 11 million farm families keep fewer than ten animals, and only around 3 percent of milk is processed through formal channels. In contrast, successful models like India's Amul and Bangladesh's Milk Vita demonstrated how rural producers can organize into cooperatives to collect, process, and market milk collectively, empowering smallholders and scaling production.

Historically, Pakistan had early cooperative movements, but they were often undermined by government control and political interference. The collapse of Punjab's credit cooperatives in the early 1990s amid loan default scandals severely damaged public trust in the cooperative framework. Consequently, Pakistani dairy and crop farmers have largely operated alone without a secure legal environment for collaboration, despite informal cooperation already existing for harvest labor and water turns.

To address structural supply-side challenges, the state has introduced several initiatives. The Green Corporate Livestock Initiative, launched under the Special Investment Facilitation Council in January 2024, aims to upgrade low-yielding livestock using advanced laboratories in Okara. Additionally, the Prime Minister launched the Pakistan Animal Identification and Traceability System in July 2026 to enable animal insurance, financing, and certification for premium export markets.

stories.title: India-UK Investment Treaty Talks Stall Over Arbitration and Tax
stories.summary:
India does not plan to aggressively pursue a bilateral investment treaty with Britain in the near term because disagreements regarding taxation and international arbitration continue to stall negotiations, according to two senior government officials. New Delhi aims to protect its sovereign right to set tax and regulatory policies, whereas Britain seeks stronger investor protections and easier access to international arbitration. These unresolved differences prevented the treaty from being finalized alongside the countries' free trade agreement, which took effect on July 15.

The hesitation reflects India's broader strategy to limit exposure to international legal challenges following high-profile arbitration disputes. British firms, including Vodafone and Cairn, previously won international arbitration cases against India concerning retrospective tax claims and canceled contracts worth billions of dollars. About a decade ago, India allowed treaties with more than 50 countries to lapse and introduced a restrictive investment law, which is currently undergoing review. Under a 2015 model treaty framework, India requires foreign investors to exhaust local legal remedies before pursuing international arbitration, though the mandatory waiting period may be shortened from five years to two or three years.

Despite the stalled investment pact, the UK remains an important economic partner, ranking as India's ninth-largest source of foreign direct investment equity inflows in 2025/26 with investments exceeding $1 billion. Officials from both nations are scheduled to meet in early December for the UK-India Economic and Financial Dialogue, co-chaired by India's finance minister and British Chancellor of the Exchequer under UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government. However, sources indicate the investment treaty will not be discussed during this ministerial forum.

Bilateral tensions have also been heightened by India's recent imposition of a 162.5 percent import duty on bulk Scotch whisky, triggering a dispute with liquor companies like Pernod Ricard and Diageo. Meanwhile, India continues negotiations on free trade agreements with at least eight countries alongside parallel investment treaty discussions with several of them, having signed revised agreements under its updated framework with nations such as the United Arab Emirates, Uzbekistan, Israel, Belarus, and Kyrgyzstan.

stories.title: Pakistani Pilot Becomes First Foreign Astronaut on China's Tiangong Station
stories.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a forty-year-old former Pakistan Air Force pilot, has achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign astronaut to join a crewed mission on China's Tiangong space station. Arriving on November 25, 2026, aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, Ali joined Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi for a mission designed to advance bilateral scientific cooperation between Pakistan and China.

Selected in April 2026, Ali spent seven months undergoing rigorous preparation at the Astronaut Centre of China in Beijing. His training encompassed spacecraft systems, emergency responses, scientific procedures, and intensive Chinese-language instruction to facilitate communication with his crewmates. Serving as a payload specialist, Ali is tasked with conducting four joint research projects selected from over three hundred proposals submitted to Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.

The scientific projects focus on materials science and biotechnology, including lightweight graphene-based radiation shields, self-healing carbon-fibre composites, and the cultivation of quinoa seeds, microalgae, and cyanobacteria in microgravity. These experiments aim to improve spacecraft durability and support sustainable food and oxygen production for extended space missions. China arranged specially prepared halal meals and bilingual operating manuals to support his stay.

Ali's mission is scheduled to last between five and ten days in orbit. In a unique logistical arrangement, he is not expected to return on the spacecraft that brought him; instead, he will travel back to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft alongside Chinese astronauts Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying. This milestone highlights decades of space collaboration between Pakistan and China, laying the groundwork for potential future joint endeavors beyond Earth.

stories.title: Pakistan Urges UN Security Council to Implement AI Military Guardrails
stories.summary:
Pakistan has called upon the United Nations Security Council to institute strict international regulatory frameworks and guardrails to prevent emerging technologies and artificial intelligence from triggering a destabilizing arms race. Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, Pakistan's permanent representative to the UN, addressed a high-level 15-member Council debate on emerging technologies and conflict resolution under the Latvian presidency, emphasizing that nuclear launch decisions must strictly remain under human control.

During the session, the Pakistani envoy stressed the critical need for military restraint and confidence-building measures to mitigate the dangers of miscalculation and compressed decision-making timelines caused by integrating AI into military operations. He specifically demanded an absolute prohibition against employing AI capabilities to target nuclear command, control, and communications systems, warning that algorithms should never be used to compress human judgment during crises.

United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres echoed these concerns at the outset of the meeting, noting that modern wars have become testing grounds for AI-enabled targeting and intelligence gathering. Guterres stressed that as long as nuclear weapons exist, the decision to use them must rest exclusively with human beings, adding that killer robots must have no place in the future. He also reiterated his urgent call to launch negotiations for a legally binding instrument addressing lethal autonomous weapon systems.

Furthermore, the UN chief highlighted that the rapid, uncontrolled race for AI is being driven by commercial interests and geopolitical rivalry, while the massive energy and water consumption of AI data centers inflames community tensions. He stated that the Security Council holds a special duty to ensure technological competition does not destabilize international peace, asserting that countries wielding the greatest AI capabilities carry the heaviest responsibilities.

stories.title: Oil Tankers Explode After Striking Naval Mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary:
Two oil tankers suffered explosions and caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to a statement from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy carried by state media. Iranian military officials asserted that the vessels were navigating through an unauthorized route within the vital waterway. The incident underscores heightened risks in the region as Tehran tightens control over maritime traffic.

In a related development, Iranian Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia announced that the military has deployed new surveillance systems and upgraded existing equipment to monitor the strait. Akraminia warned that ships attempting passage without coordinating directly with Iranian forces face severe hazards, noting that vessels failing to cooperate have struck mines during recent weeks.

Tehran has communicated to Washington that normal shipping operations will not resume in the Strait of Hormuz until specific conditions are met. Iran's demands include the termination of the U.S. naval blockade targeting Iranian ports and an end to the ongoing war on all fronts. Transmitted through Qatari mediators, Tehran's proposal indicates readiness to reopen the vital maritime trade route within forty-eight hours should Washington fulfill these stipulated terms.

stories.title: Indian Equities Surge Toward Annual Recovery Amid Massive Foreign Inflows
stories.summary:
Indian stock markets rallied on Wednesday, nearly wiping out their year-to-date losses and positioning the benchmarks for their strongest monthly performance since April 2020. The market surge has been driven by lower oil prices, strong corporate earnings, and a massive influx of foreign capital. Investors poured a record $14.28 billion into Indian equities this month as funds rotated away from global artificial intelligence-linked shares.

The broader market gains lifted the Nifty 50 by 1.85 percent to close at 25,819.25, while the Sensex rose 1.82 percent to settle at 83,938.28 following a local holiday on Tuesday. Meanwhile, the Indian rupee recovered from historic lows, appreciating by up to 2.9 percent over the course of the month. These gains contrasted sharply with the broader MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan, which fell 3.3 percent amid renewed concerns over prospective United States tariffs and a fading technology rally.

India emerged as Asia's top-performing market for the month, with the Nifty 50 gaining more than 15 percent in dollar terms. Analysts noted that strong earnings momentum, low foreign positioning, and insulation from AI market concentration make India an attractive hedge. Economists forecast a 7.6 percent growth rate for the Indian economy during the July-September quarter, matching corporate earnings that reached a four-year high for the same period.

Sector-wide advances bolstered the market, with heavyweight financials and information technology posting notable increases. HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank climbed 3.5 percent and 3.4 percent respectively, while Reliance Industries added 1.7 percent. Concurrently, Brent crude futures declined slightly to $91 per barrel due to rising supply expectations, contributing to a monthly price drop of approximately 22.5 percent.

stories.title: MQM-P Files for Permission to Hold Karachi Rally for Urban Province
stories.summary:
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan formally applied for administrative permission on Wednesday to hold a public rally and gathering at Jinnah Ground in Karachi. Taha Ahmed Khan, the party's deputy parliamentary leader, submitted the official request for a No-Objection Certificate to Karachi Commissioner Hassan Naqvi for the proposed event scheduled for November 29.

In the formal application, MQM-P asked the city administration to provide necessary security and administrative support to ensure the peaceful execution of the gathering. The primary objective of the November 29 rally is to mobilize public backing for the creation of a new province representing urban Sindh.

Meanwhile, the ruling Pakistan Peoples Party has initiated discussions with various nationalist factions and the MQM-P. The PPP has urged these political entities to postpone their planned rallies and public demonstrations on November 29 to mitigate the risk of potential political clashes within the region.

stories.title: Twelve Bangladeshi Cricketers Register For Upcoming IPL Mini Auction
stories.summary:
Organisers reported on Wednesday that twelve cricketers from Bangladesh have officially registered for the upcoming Indian Premier League auction scheduled for next month. These players are included in the initial roster of 1,220 candidates for the December 16 mini auction in Goa, though the pool will be narrowed down before franchises make their final picks, according to the Board of Control for Cricket in India. The BCCI noted that with 184 athletes already retained or selected by teams ahead of the event, a maximum of 66 slots, including 25 overseas positions, remain open.

This development occurs despite tense political relations between India and Bangladesh. Bangladesh was previously excluded from the Twenty20 World Cup co-hosted by India following a refusal to play matches on Indian soil due to security concerns. That incident followed an order by the BCCI instructing the Kolkata Knight Riders to drop Bangladeshi fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman despite a purchase of over $1 million during the previous year's auction. Those events coincided with online demonstrations by right-wing groups in India referencing alleged violence against Hindus in Muslim-majority Bangladesh, while Dhaka asserted that Indian media exaggerated the scale of those incidents.

Bilateral ties have worsened significantly following a 2024 mass uprising in Bangladesh that removed former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, a close ally of New Delhi who is currently living in exile in India. Meanwhile, the broader IPL registration list features high-profile figures such as England all-rounder Ben Stokes with a base price of $216,900. Indian players form the majority of the initial pool with 939 entries, while Australia leads the international contingent with 53 players, followed by South Africa, the West Indies, New Zealand, and Afghanistan. Emerging cricket nations are also represented, including thirteen registrations from the United States and ten each from Nepal and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Prime Minister Commends Climate Minister For SCO Civilizational Dialogue
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Minister for Climate Change Musadik Malik in Islamabad to commend his diplomatic efforts. The Prime Minister praised Malik for representing Pakistan effectively during the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilizational Dialogue held in Delhi.

During the meeting, the Prime Minister highlighted that Malik accurately conveyed historical contexts and ground realities during the regional dialogue. Furthermore, Sharif commended Malik's eloquence, proficiency in the Urdu language, and his ability to communicate complex matters clearly.

Sharif stated that Malik established a new benchmark for diplomatic engagement through his intellectual clarity and patience. According to the Prime Minister, these qualities successfully contributed to projecting a positive image of Pakistan throughout the region.

The interaction underscores the government's recognition of ministerial performance in international forums. No further details regarding the discussions were mentioned in the official reports.

stories.title: Maldives And Pakistan Agree To Expand Bilateral Ties And Launch Flights
stories.summary:
Pakistan and the Maldives have formally agreed to broaden their bilateral cooperation across multiple sectors, including tourism, health, trade, sports, and manpower. The agreement was reached during a meeting in Islamabad involving Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State Talal Chaudhry, and Maldivian Minister of Tourism and Civil Aviation Mohamed Ameen.

During the discussions, Naqvi noted that Islamabad possesses substantial potential to serve as a tourism capital. Ameen announced plans for the national airline of the Maldives to initiate direct flights connecting Pakistan and the Maldivian islands, a move designed to simplify travel for Pakistani citizens. Naqvi emphasized that the new air links would increase the flow of Pakistani tourists to the Maldives, mentioning that prominent Pakistani artists, celebrities, and cricket stars intend to travel on the inaugural direct flight. Ameen concurred that popular Pakistani public figures visiting the island nation would significantly support tourism promotion.

In addition to tourism and aviation initiatives, Naqvi shared that the Pakistan Cricket Board is currently formulating a project to construct a cricket academy and stadium in the Maldives to offer improved training facilities for local youth. Addressing economic cooperation, Ameen stated that the Maldives requires additional workforce and would enthusiastically welcome workers from Pakistan. He also pointed out extensive commercial opportunities for importing construction supplies, pharmaceutical products, and other commodities from Pakistan.

stories.title: FIFA Presidential Hopeful Kozo Tashima Pledges Single Term If Elected
stories.summary:
FIFA presidential candidate Kozo Tashima announced on Wednesday that he intends to limit his tenure to a single four-year term if he defeats current president Gianni Infantino and French football leader Philippe Diallo in the upcoming March election. Tashima, representing Japan, has committed to restoring integrity and transparency to world football's governing body, positioning himself as one of three contenders on the ballot.

Infantino faces substantial criticism over a controversial and ultimately aborted proposal to permit private investment into the World Cup, yet he maintains robust backing for his bid to secure a fourth and final term. Acknowledging that his prospects of winning are relatively slim, the 69-year-old Tashima outlined his brief agenda to reporters in Tokyo, emphasizing that his four-year focus would center entirely on overhauling governance and making internal administrative processes within FIFA more transparent.

Tashima previously stated that he was not considering withdrawing from the race to clear a direct path for Diallo to challenge Infantino. Diallo currently holds the backing of Europe and is widely viewed as the more formidable challenger to unseat the incumbent president. Tashima confirmed he has spoken with Diallo via telephone and plans an in-person meeting in Europe to discuss tactical alignment.

While noting that he and Diallo share a similar overarching direction, Tashima indicated that further communication would determine whether their strategies completely align or retain distinct differences. Ultimately, Tashima stressed that their primary objective is returning FIFA to the proper course, utilizing various tactical options to reach that goal.

stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Approves NCCIA Restructuring Plan
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered a comprehensive modernisation of the country's cybercrime prevention system and approved the restructuring of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency. During a high-level meeting in Islamabad, the premier reviewed the agency's administrative structure, future strategy, and performance, emphasizing that protecting the public from cybercrime is among the government's top priorities.

The prime minister directed that the NCCIA be transformed into an effective, proactive, and modern institution by recruiting the best available workforce strictly on merit. He specifically ordered the appointment of artificial intelligence and information technology experts across the agency and all its subordinate offices, utilizing modern technology and all available resources to resolve pending cybercrime cases.

To oversee the transition, Prime Minister Sharif formed a special committee consisting of Federal Ministers Mohsin Naqvi, Azam Nazeer Tarar, Muhammad Aurangzeb, and Shaza Fatima Khawaja. This committee is tasked with reviewing reform proposals and submitting formal recommendations to the prime minister by the end of the week. Officials were also informed about a proposal to convert the agency into a national-level Pakistan Cyber Police alongside the operationalization of a dedicated national security cybercrime system.

The meeting was attended by several senior federal ministers, ministers of state, and relevant institutional officials. The restructuring initiative follows recent agency disclosures regarding massive financial networks involved in illegal online gambling, fraudulent business operations, and suspected money laundering, alongside ongoing internal concerns regarding staff shortages.

stories.title: Timeline of Spain, Portugal, and Morocco's 2030 World Cup Bid
stories.summary:
Spain, Portugal, and Morocco successfully secured the hosting rights for the 2030 FIFA World Cup following a multi-year collaborative process that united European and African football federations. The joint candidacy originated when Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and Portuguese counterpart Antonio Costa agreed to explore a joint bid, with Sanchez subsequently inviting Morocco to join in order to enhance their chances of winning.

Initially, the Royal Spanish Football Federation and the Portuguese Football Federation started analyzing a joint bid without Morocco, later formally presenting a proposal to FIFA featuring multiple host cities across Spain and Portugal. The bid briefly expanded when Ukraine joined the candidacy as a gesture of solidarity following the Russian invasion earlier that year, though Ukraine's role was later left to be clarified due to ongoing wartime circumstances.

A major shift occurred during the FIFA Congress in Rwanda, where an official announcement confirmed that Morocco had joined the Spain-Portugal bid to form a powerful bi-continental candidacy uniting Europe and Africa. Reports noted that Morocco had originally been omitted due to initial doubts regarding UEFA backing, but talks resumed after other European bids withdrew.

The FIFA Council eventually designated the joint Spain, Portugal, and Morocco bid as the sole candidate for the tournament. Additionally, FIFA announced that Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay would each host a single match to mark the centenary of the first World Cup held in Uruguay in 1930. Ultimately, the FIFA Congress formally ratified Spain, Portugal, and Morocco as the primary hosts, granting all six participating host nations automatic qualification.

stories.title: CAS Reinstates Senegal as African Champions Over Morocco Appeal
stories.summary:
Senegal has been officially reinstated as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against a previous decision to strip them of the title. The CAS panel set aside the Confederation of African Football Appeal Board's ruling that had earlier forfeited Senegal's 1-0 extra-time victory and awarded Morocco a 3-0 win, confirming the original final score in Rabat as 1-0 in favor of Senegal.

The legal dispute stemmed from the final match during which Senegal briefly walked off the pitch for 14 minutes following a late penalty awarded against them. The players subsequently returned, Morocco missed the spot kick, and Pape Gueye scored the winning goal in extra time. The CAS panel ruled that the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, committed no error of law and that his decision to resume the match fell strictly within the 'field of play' doctrine under his sole authority.

Senesgalese Football Federation President Abdoulaye Fall praised the verdict as a triumph for sporting fairness, emphasizing the bonds of brotherhood shared with the Royal Moroccan Football Federation. Meanwhile, the FRMF announced plans to challenge the CAS decision by initiating legal proceedings before the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, alleging improper contact between the Senesgalese federation and a CAS arbitrator prior to the ruling. Both the federation and the implicated arbitrator strongly denied the allegations of direct contact.

Senior sports law experts chaired the arbitration panel, which also noted that CAF had already imposed separate disciplinary sanctions on various Senesgalese players and officials. Players such as Sadio Mane expressed hope that the legal battle would not create lasting division between the two nations, emphasizing mutual respect and the unifying power of football.

stories.title: Lahore Police Crack Down on Underage Drivers with Fines and Impoundments
stories.summary:
Lahore Traffic Police have initiated a stringent enforcement campaign targeting underage drivers, ordering the immediate seizure of motorcycles, cars, and rickshaws operated by minors throughout the city. According to the Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) of Lahore, owners and underage operators face substantial financial penalties for breaking traffic rules, and confiscated vehicles will only be returned once parents provide a surety bond.

Authorities have issued a warning that repeat offenses by minors will result in the filing of official criminal charges against them. Official statistics indicate that traffic personnel have issued 23,440 challans to underage motorists across Lahore since the beginning of the year. The CTO urged parents to demonstrate greater responsibility and prevent minors from operating motor vehicles to protect public safety and reduce collisions.

This crackdown follows a tragic incident last year in the Shahdara area of Lahore, where a juvenile motorist lost control of an automobile and plowed into three motorcycles. The crash resulted in the death of 30-year-old Muhammad Amin and left three others injured. The victim's brother filed a formal complaint that led to the registration of a case, and the juvenile driver, named Hashir, was subsequently arrested and charged.

Following the fatal accident, Punjab Police Inspector General Dr. Usman Anwar intervened and voiced severe concern over traffic violations committed by minors. The ongoing police measures aim to curb reckless driving habits among youths and enforce strict adherence to municipal traffic laws across the urban area.

stories.title: Iran Defends Trade Resilience Against US Blockade While Combating Inflation
stories.summary:
Iran's first vice president announced on Wednesday that Tehran remains unconcerned regarding a United States naval blockade, highlighting a substantial surge in cargo processing through alternative borders. Speaking in Dubai, Mohammad Reza Aref stated that the increased unloading and clearance of merchandise via non-southern entry points demonstrates the country's capacity to bypass naval restrictions.

The administration is currently dealing with severe inflation driven by a prolonged conflict, which has triggered sharp spikes in the cost of basic consumer goods and food products. Official data from the Statistical Centre of Iran shows that overall consumer prices in October climbed 88.7% compared to the previous year, while annual average inflation reached 76.8% and food and beverage expenses surged by 112.6%.

Despite these economic challenges, Aref asserted that strategic goods reserves remain robust and supplies are plentiful, though he did not provide specific figures. He also noted that the government aims to suppress basic commodity price increases for a minimum duration of three months. The US recently reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports in July and established Task Force Iron Gate to monitor land and Caspian Sea borders.

In a separate gathering, President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized that the administration intends to channel additional budgetary resources and energy savings toward enhancing living standards for impoverished populations. The measures form part of broader efforts by Iranian authorities to stabilize domestic markets and support vulnerable communities amidst severe economic pressures.

stories.title: Pakistan Temporarily Closes Multiple Air Routes for Two Days
stories.summary:
Aviation authorities in Pakistan have announced the temporary closure of several air routes situated inside the Lahore Flight Information Region (FIR). The restrictions, implemented for operational reasons, are scheduled for November 25 and 26.

A Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) indicates that the affected airspace will remain restricted daily from 5:30 am to 9:30 am. The closures apply from ground level up to an unlimited altitude and impact numerous specific routes, including A466, N644, P500, M881, G201, G202, L750, G326, J139, J119, J124, J138, J141, J145, J164, J165, J153, J116, and J166.

To maintain continuous flight operations during the closure window, authorities have designated five alternative air routes. Furthermore, the NOTAM outlines specific alternative climb and descent paths for flights operating to and from Multan, Faisalabad, and Dera Ismail Khan.

Under the temporary directives, aircraft utilizing the alternative corridors must adhere to designated altitude restrictions. While the primary routes are unavailable due to operational necessities, the alternative pathways ensure ongoing air traffic movement across the region.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court Blocks Deportation of Afghan Medical Graduates
stories.summary:
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) issued an order on Wednesday preventing authorities from deporting eight Afghan medical students from the country. A division bench composed of Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Farah Jamshed reviewed a legal challenge filed against the termination of these Afghan graduates from their mandatory house jobs following the completion of their medical degrees in Pakistan.

During the proceedings, the legal representative for the petitioners argued that preventing the students from finishing their required house jobs would render their four years of medical studies in Pakistan entirely pointless. Counsel further explained that the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) had previously issued directives for the deportation of the scholars. After hearing initial arguments, the bench halted the expulsion of the eight individuals, requested responses from all involved respondents, and adjourned the case.

A similar legal intervention occurred previously in the Lahore High Court, where Justice Khalid Ishaq paused the execution of PMDC notifications that mandated the removal of Afghan scholars from medical and educational institutions. That case involved 30 Afghan students, including Syed Mobeen Ulfati, challenging orders dated July 31 and September 1. The court directed notices to the federal government and the PMDC, requiring replies by September 18 after questioning how the students were admitted if their visas were allegedly invalid.

The disputes follow a broader PMDC directive prohibiting new admissions, placements, migrations, or transfers of Afghan nationals in medical and dental colleges throughout Pakistan. The council also instructed educational institutions to facilitate the return of already enrolled Afghan nationals to Afghanistan according to prevailing government policy. These actions align with Pakistan's wider repatriation initiative targeting undocumented foreign nationals, which commenced in 2023 and expanded in 2025 and 2026 under the Illegal Foreigners' Repatriation Plan, resulting in the deportation of over one million Afghan nationals.

stories.title: Pakistan and China Agree on Government-to-Government Fuel Storage Arrangements
stories.summary:
Pakistan and China have agreed to pursue government-to-government arrangements for Chinese investment in petrol and liquefied petroleum gas storage and terminal facilities in Pakistan. Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Pakistan State Oil Chief Executive Officer Jawwad Ahmed Cheema met with Chinese ambassador Jiang Zaidong and his commercial team in Islamabad to explore investment opportunities across the energy and mining sectors.

The two nations identified two primary areas for early action. The first priority involves an LPG plant alongside storage and terminal facilities aimed at boosting domestic supply, improving cleaner fuel access, and easing shortages during peak seasons. The second involves motor gasoline imports, covering sourcing, storage, and logistics to reinforce fuel security. A joint commercial team of representatives from both countries will be formed to evaluate opportunities and develop a structured project roadmap.

Minister Malik encouraged Chinese investment across upstream, offshore, minerals, mining, and downstream energy infrastructure, pointing to investor-friendly policies and petroleum sector deregulation. The minister also congratulated Pakistan Air Force Wing Commander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali for his participation in China's Shenzhou-24 space mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, marking him as the first Pakistani in orbit and first foreign visitor to the Tiangong space station.

Ambassador Jiang reaffirmed China's support and expressed keen interest in strengthening business-to-business linkages. The engagement builds upon recent discussions at the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen and aims to translate bilateral cooperation into lasting economic gains for both countries.

stories.title: بلاول بھٹو کا مولانا فضل الرحمان کی رہائش گاہ کے محاصرے پر اظہار یکجہتی
stories.summary:
چیئرمین پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی بلاول بھٹو زرداری نے جمعیت علمائے اسلام کے سربراہ مولانا فضل الرحمٰن سے ٹیلی فون پر رابطہ کیا ہے۔ اس گفتگو کے دوران مولانا فضل الرحمٰن نے چیئرمین پیپلز پارٹی کو لاہور میں اپنی رہائش گاہ کے پولیس محاصرے کے حوالے سے تفصیلات سے آگاہ کیا۔ بلاول بھٹو نے مولانا فضل الرحمٰن کی رہائش گاہ کے اس محاصرے پر ان کے ساتھ بھرپور اظہار یکجہتی کیا۔

اس ٹیلی فونک رابطے سے چند روز قبل بھی بلاول بھٹو زرداری جمعیت علمائے اسلام کے خلاف کیے جانے والے حکومتی اقدامات اور سیاسی انتقام کا نشانہ بنائے جانے کی شدید مذمت کر چکے ہیں۔ اس موقع پر ان کا کہنا تھا کہ حکومت کو اپوزیشن کی طرف سے کی جانے والی تنقید کو خندہ پیشانی سے برداشت کرنا چاہیے۔

بلاول بھٹو نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ ایک جمہوری اور پارلیمانی نظام کے اندر ذمے دار اپوزیشن کا کردار انتہائی اہم ہوتا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ حکومت کو ایسے کسی بھی اقدام سے گریز کرنا چاہیے جس سے جمہوریت اور پارلیمان کو کسی بھی قسم کا نقصان پہنچے یا وہ کمزور ہوں۔

واضح رہے کہ اس صورتحال کے تناظر میں لاہور میں جمعیت علمائے اسلام کے سربراہ مولانا فضل الرحمان کی قیام گاہ کی طرف جانے والے راستوں سے کنٹینرز ہٹا دیے گئے تھے اور شام چھ بجے ان راستوں کو ٹریفک کے لیے کھول دیا گیا تھا۔

stories.title: Teenage Batter Sooryavanshi Breaks Records After Yuvraj Singh Mentorship
stories.summary:
Fifteen-year-old Indian cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored a record-breaking 204 runs off 53 balls against the United Arab Emirates in Doha during the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament. His explosive innings powered India A to a seven-wicket victory after chasing a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs, finishing with a strike rate of 384.90 and 28 sixes.

Sooryavanshi achieved the fastest century and double century in List A cricket. He reached his hundred in 28 deliveries, beating Australia’s Jake Fraser-McGurk, and secured his double century in 52 balls, eclipsing Chad Bowes' previous mark of 103 deliveries. The teenager credited a half-hour mentoring session with his idol, former India international Yuvraj Singh, for helping him correct technical flaws after two earlier disappointing performances.

Reflecting on his innings, Sooryavanshi explained that reviewing match videos alongside Yuvraj's advice helped him identify mistakes. Recognizing that the pitch in Doha favored an attacking approach and allowed the ball to come onto the bat nicely, he decided to back his strengths rather than struggle to adjust his approach as he had in previous matches.

The young batter has previously made headlines by becoming India's youngest men’s international during a T20 debut against England in Manchester, surpassing a record held by Sachin Tendulkar. He also finished as the leading run-scorer in this year's Indian Premier League season with the Rajasthan Royals, accumulating 776 runs at a strike rate of 237.30.

stories.title: Usman Khawaja Expresses Disappointment Over Pat Cummins' Sandpapergate Denials
stories.summary:
Retired Australian opener Usman Khawaja has stated he was disappointed by Test captain Pat Cummins' denials regarding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, commonly known as Sandpapergate. Khawaja recently claimed in his autobiography that the entire team was aware of the plot, whereas official Cricket Australia findings previously placed responsibility solely on Steve Smith, David Warner, and Cameron Bancroft.

Khawaja clarified that he never wanted Cummins to lose his captaincy, stating he reached out to Cummins prior to a recent press conference in hopes of finding a middle ground and accepting collective responsibility. Instead, Cummins strongly denied any involvement and criticized Khawaja's delayed claims as casual and potentially defamatory. Khawaja expressed surprise at the personal nature of Cummins' response, noting he had never seen that side of the captain before.

While Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening the 2018 investigation, it established a forum for players to share their experiences from that period. Khawaja proposed a compromise statement to CA Chief Executive Todd Greenberg, suggesting the team acknowledge collective knowledge of artificial ball alteration regardless of whether sandpaper specifically was used, though Greenberg doubted the proposal would succeed.

Khawaja, whose version of events has received backing from Warner and Bancroft, maintained that he has told the truth and stands by his account. Meanwhile, Cummins received the unanimous support of Cricket Australia to retain his position as captain following the renewed controversy.

stories.title: Pakistan Secures Tuna Quota and Invites Maldivian Investment in Fisheries
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry invited the Maldives to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan's tuna-processing and canning industry. The invitation was extended during a meeting in Pakistan with an eight-member Maldivian delegation led by Minister of Tourism and Civil Aviation Mohamed Ameen, aimed at strengthening trade, transport links, and the blue economy.

Minister Chaudhry announced that Pakistan has secured a tuna quota of 25,000 metric tonnes from the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission for the first time. This allocation includes 15,000 tonnes of yellowfin tuna and 10,000 tonnes of skipjack, which is projected to generate roughly $200 million in export earnings. He noted that sustainable fishing practices and policy reforms can help expand exports, attract foreign investment, and protect marine resources.

Both sides also discussed expanding cooperation into areas such as medical tourism, food security, and medical equipment. A joint working group has been established to identify trade opportunities and formulate recommendations to facilitate bilateral trade and investment ahead of a high-level Pakistani delegation's visit to the Maldives in December.

The Maldivian delegation visiting Pakistan also included Deputy Minister of Tourism and Civil Aviation Mohamed Awadh, Maldivian High Commissioner to Pakistan Mohamed Thoha, and senior aviation officials. The discussions emphasized mutual economic growth and closer institutional coordination between the two nations.

stories.title: Karachi Air Quality Reaches Very Unhealthy Levels Amid Rising Pollution
stories.summary:
Karachi has recorded an Air Quality Index reading of 236, making it the second most polluted city globally according to a recent report from a global environmental monitoring website. This high figure places the city's air into the very unhealthy bracket, where fine particulate matter concentrations greatly exceed safety thresholds recommended by the World Health Organization. Meteorological factors, notably cooler temperatures combined with slower wind speeds, have worsened the crisis by trapping airborne pollutants and preventing them from dispersing across the atmosphere.

Medical professionals caution that breathing this contaminated air creates severe health hazards for local inhabitants, potentially leading to persistent respiratory complications, throat irritation, allergic reactions, and sore eyes. Specialists strongly advise vulnerable demographics, including young children, senior citizens, and people suffering from asthma or other chronic respiratory illnesses, to steer clear of non-essential outdoor excursions. Additionally, members of the public are urged to utilize protective face masks whenever traveling outside to limit their direct inhalation of dangerous airborne contaminants.

In related national developments, federal authorities and the Pakistan Peoples Party have reached a consensus regarding the scheduling of a National Assembly session following recent discussions between the two factions. Information from party insiders indicates that the upcoming parliamentary meeting will likely be convened on December 1, with the administration having briefed the PPP on the matter.

Monitoring environmental conditions and air quality remains crucial as winter weather patterns continue to trap pollutants in major urban centers across the region. Health officials emphasize that adherence to personal safety measures, such as wearing masks and minimizing outdoor exposure during peak pollution hours, is essential for mitigating immediate health risks while long-term mitigation strategies are evaluated.

stories.title: South Korean Equities Fall Sharply Following Tech Slump on Wall Street
stories.summary:
South Korean financial markets experienced a significant downturn as local share prices dropped steeply in the wake of an overnight technology stock selloff on Wall Street. The sharp decline was driven by renewed skepticism regarding the long-term viability of artificial intelligence investments, alongside widespread profit-taking by market participants following recent gains. Amidst the equity selloff, the local currency strengthened against the US dollar, while benchmark bond yields experienced a downward movement.

According to analysts at Shinhan Investment & Securities, investors are also weighing potential risks associated with future US tariffs alongside the ongoing correction in technology shares. Major index components bore the brunt of the losses, with prominent chipmaker Samsung Electronics falling 8 percent and industry peer SK Hynix dropping 7.51 percent. Other prominent market heavyweights, including battery manufacturer LG Energy Solution and automakers Hyundai Motor and Kia Corp, also posted negative or flat returns during the trading session.

Foreign investors acted as net sellers, offloading shares totaling 1.016 trillion won. Meanwhile, the won was quoted at 1,341.6 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, marking a slight increase compared to its previous close. In the broader fixed-income sector, yields on three-year Korean treasury bonds edged slightly higher, whereas the benchmark ten-year yield decreased by 3.2 basis points.

Despite the sharp single-day correction, the broader market indicators reflect positive performance over the course of the year. The benchmark KOSPI index retains a substantial gain for the year to date, and the national currency has similarly appreciated against the dollar over the same timeframe, demonstrating underlying resilience despite external pressures from global tech sector volatility.

stories.title: Pakistan Military Lauds China for Historic First Human Spaceflight Mission
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s military leadership has formally expressed deep gratitude to China for its crucial backing in executing the nation's inaugural human spaceflight mission. Key defense figures, including Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Naval Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, and National Strategic Command Commander General Syed Aamer Raza, shared their congratulations with the nation, SUPARCO, and scientific teams.

The landmark expedition features Wing Commander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who becomes Pakistan's first astronaut and the initial foreign space traveler to visit China’s Tiangong Space Station. The Inter-Services Public Relations highlighted the event as a monumental step in technological advancement, demonstrating the potential of the country's human capital and inspiring younger generations.

The military praised the scientists, engineers, and technical personnel of SUPARCO for their sustained professionalism and dedication. Officials underscored that the deep-rooted partnership between Islamabad and Beijing has now expanded from terrestrial bounds into outer space, reaching unprecedented heights.

Meanwhile, environmental updates noted a severe decline in air quality elsewhere in the country. Karachi recorded an Air Quality Index of 236, propelling the city to the second most polluted globally and placing its atmosphere into the very unhealthy category according to a global monitoring website.

stories.title: Pakistan Cricket Board Names 15-Player Squad for Upcoming West Indies Series
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has revealed a 15-member national women's team for an upcoming white-ball tour to the West Indies, scheduled for next month. All-rounder Fatima Sana will captain the squad, which features a series of three Twenty20 Internationals followed by three One-Day Internationals that count toward the ICC Women’s Championship for the 2025 to 2029 cycle.

Matches are set to take place at Windsor Park in Roseau, running from December 8 through December 20. The T20I matches are scheduled for December 8, 10, and 12, with the ODI fixtures following on December 15, 17, and 20. Pakistan currently sits fifth in the championship standings, having secured five victories across nine matches.

Captain Fatima Sana missed the recent ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy due to participation in her debut season of the Women’s Big Bash League in Australia. The selected roster includes Ayesha Zafar, Gull Feroza, Momina Riasat, Muneeba Ali, Najiha Alvi, Nashra Sundhu, Sadaf Shamas, Shawaal Zulfiqar, Sidra Amin, Syeda Aroob Shah, Tasmia Rubab, Tuba Hassan, Umm-e-Hani, and Waheeda Akhtar.

The team coaching and support staff features head coach Shane Deitz, team manager Ayesha Ashhar, spin bowling coach Abdur Rehman, fast bowling coach Umaid Asif, fielding coach Abdul Majeed, batting coach Imran Farhat, performance analyst Waleed Ahmed, strength and conditioning coach Moeen, and physiotherapist Dur Samand.

stories.title: Saudi Tourism Ministry Introduces Five Digital Services via Tawakkalna Application
stories.summary:
Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Tourism has integrated five distinct digital services into the unified national application, Tawakkalna. This initiative is designed to bolster digital integration, streamline beneficiary access, and improve overall service delivery efficiency in alignment with the Kingdom's evolving tourism sector.

The rollout reflects the ministry's commitment to aligning with Digital Government Authority guidelines and expanding official access channels. The newly incorporated services allow users to apply for tour guide licenses, manage ministry licenses and applications, handle tour guiding training, review training applications along with issued certificates, and verify lists of licensed individuals and entities.

These functions link directly with the broader Tourism Platform established by the ministry to create a cohesive digital ecosystem. Users can submit requests through the app, which subsequent ministry systems then process to maintain operational continuity across different digital platforms.

The ministry emphasized that launching these features on Tawakkalna represents a major stride in cooperation with other governmental bodies, specifically the Digital Government Authority. Continued partnership aims to advance digital infrastructure and fulfill the strategic vision of Saudi Vision 2030.

stories.title: Punjab Minister Criticizes JUI-F Chief Over Remarks Targeting State Institutions
stories.summary:
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari publicly criticized Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman for making inappropriate statements and inciting violence against a national institution. Speaking on the detention of the JUI-F leader, Bokhari stated that government action was taken based on law and order considerations, arguing that the politician had crossed multiple red lines through recent video remarks and taunts regarding military salaries.

Bokhari emphasized that despite official respect for Fazlur Rehman as an elder, and ongoing efforts by cabinet ministers to defuse his anger, threatening the armed forces is unacceptable. She questioned whether the country was a banana republic where threats could be leveraged to force government compliance without dialogue.

Simultaneously, the Lahore High Court intervened regarding the situation, instructing the Capital City Police Officer of Lahore to submit a comprehensive report. Justice Ali Zia Bajwa heard a petition filed by lawyer Abrar Hussain concerning the alleged detention, warning that unlawful detention would carry serious consequences for responsible parties.

The petitioner sought judicial intervention to ensure the safety and recovery of the JUI-F chief, prompting the court to demand formal justifications for any restrictive measures taken against his liberty.

stories.title: Pakistani Astronaut Zeeshan Ali Reaches Space Aboard Shenzhou-24 Spacecraft
stories.summary:
China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, carrying a three-person crew consisting of Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi alongside 40-year-old Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Propelled by a Long March 2-F rocket, the mission marked a historic milestone for Pakistan as its first astronaut entered space. Broadcast screens at the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission headquarters in Islamabad displayed the launch live as citizens gathered to watch the departure.

Following its successful liftoff, the spacecraft completed its journey and docked with the Tiangong space station's forward port approximately three hours and 38 minutes after launch. The docking procedure proceeded smoothly, initiating a new chapter of international cooperation in space exploration. Following the successful arrival at the orbiting laboratory, the newly arrived crew members met with the existing occupants, leading to a joint group photograph of the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 teams inside the station.

The mission has drawn widespread acclaim and excitement across Pakistan, symbolizing a monumental leap for the nation's scientific achievements. Public reactions have highlighted the strong partnership between Pakistan and China in aerospace technology, with many viewing the successful flight as a realization of a long-held national dream as the crew begins their scheduled duties aboard the orbital outpost.

stories.title: کراچی میں پانچ ہزار روپے کے جعلی نوٹوں سے فراڈ کا انکشاف
stories.summary:
کراچی میں پانچ ہزار روپے کے جعلی نوٹوں کے ذریعے ایک شہری کے ساتھ فراڈ کیے جانے کا انکشاف سامنے آیا ہے۔ ملزمان نے آن لائن اشتہار کے ذریعے ایک نوجوان سے موبائل فون خریدا اور اس کی قیمت چکانے کے لیے اسے دو لاکھ ساٹھ ہزار روپے کے جعلی نوٹ تھما دیے۔

متاثرہ نوجوان کے مطابق واردات کے دوران ملزمان نے اس کے دوست کو مبینہ طور پر کوئی مشروب پلا کر حواس باختہ کر دیا تھا۔ حکام کا کہنا ہے کہ اس دھوکہ دہی کے واقعے کے حوالے سے مزید تفتیش تاحال جاری رکھی جا رہی ہے۔

اس خبر کے علاوہ ذرائع ابلاغ میں مختلف دیگر اہم واقعات بھی زیرِ بحث رہے۔ ترجمان پولیس کے مطابق ایک ماں نے اپنی بیٹی کو باہر پھینک کر پولیس کے ہنگامی نمبر پندرہ پر اغوا کی جھوٹی کال کی۔ اس کے علاوہ سکھر میں ایک نایاب بلائنڈ ڈولفن راستہ بھٹک کر خیرپور میں علی نواز واہ آر ڈی سو کے مقام پر پہنچ گئی، جسے ریسکیو حکام نے بروقت کارروائی کرتے ہوئے بحفاظت دریائے سندھ میں واپس چھوڑ دیا۔

لاہور کے علاقے گارڈن ٹاؤن میں دو بہنوں سمیت تین افراد کے مبینہ قاتل نے خودکشی کر لی۔ پولیس ذرائع کے مطابق قیدی رانک لین کو طبیعت خراب ہونے پر اسپتال لایا گیا تھا۔ پشاور میں بائیک رائیڈرز کو قانونی دائرے میں لانے کا فیصلہ کرتے ہوئے کمشنر آفس نے ان کے لیے مخصوص روٹس اور اوقات کار مقرر کرنے کا اعلان کیا ہے۔

stories.title: کرس آرمسٹرانگ نے حادثے اور طلاق کے باوجود شوہر سے نبھایا گیا وعدہ پورا کیا
stories.summary:
کرس آرمسٹرانگ کی شادی کو محض دو سال ہوئے تھے جب ان کے شوہر برینڈن ایک شدید کار حادثے کا شکار ہو گئے۔ حادثے کے نتیجے میں برینڈن کے دماغ کو شدید چوٹ پہنچی اور وہ طویل کومے میں چلے گئے۔ ہوش میں آنے کے بعد بھی ان کی یادداشت، بولنے اور سمجھنے کی صلاحیتیں شدید متاثر ہو چکی تھیں اور وہ مکمل طور پر دوسروں پر انحصار کرنے لگے۔

ابتدائی توقعات کے برعکس برینڈن کی صحت بہتر ہونے کے بجائے وقت کے ساتھ مزید ابتر ہوتی گئی۔ ڈاکٹروں کی طرف سے ملنے والے ایک خط نے یہ واضح کر دیا کہ وہ اب کبھی کام نہیں کر سکیں گے۔ اس مشکل صورتحال میں کرس نے برینڈن کو گھر لا کر ان کی چوبیس گھنٹے دیکھ بھال شروع کی، جو ان کے لیے انتہائی تھکا دینے والا اور جذباتی طور پر توڑ دینے والا عمل ثابت ہوا۔ شدید ذہنی دباؤ اور جسمانی تھکن کے باعث بالآخر انھیں برینڈن کو ایک نرسنگ ہوم میں منتقل کرنے کا کٹھن فیصلہ کرنا پڑا۔

نرسنگ ہوم منتقل کرنے کے بعد کرس نے حالات کا گہرائی سے جائزہ لیا اور طویل مشاورت کے بعد برینڈن سے قانونی طور پر طلاق لینے کا فیصلہ کیا۔ تاہم اس طلاق کا مقصد برینڈن کو چھوڑنا نہیں بلکہ ان کی قانونی سرپرست بنے رہنا اور ان کے حقوق کے تحفظ کی جنگ جاری رکھنا تھا۔ طلاق کے بعد طویل اور پیچیدہ عدالتی کارروائی کے ذریعے کرس نے یہ کامیابی حاصل کی کہ خاندان میں سے کسی نے بھی ان کی سرپرستی کی مخالفت نہیں کی۔

برینڈن کی دیکھ بھال کی تمام تر ذمہ داریاں نبھانے کے ساتھ ساتھ کرس نے کئی سال بعد اپنی ذاتی زندگی کے بارے میں بھی سوچا۔ انہوں نے ایک آن لائن ڈیٹنگ ایپ پر پروفائل بنائی جہاں ان کی ملاقات جیمز سے ہوئی۔ کرس نے ابتدا میں ہی جیمز کو اپنے پہلے شوہر اور اپنی ذمہ داریوں کے بارے میں سب کچھ سچ سچ بتا دیا۔ جیمز نے اس صورتحال کو منفی سمجھنے کے بجائے سراہا، اور وقت کے ساتھ دونوں کے درمیان گہرے تعلقات استوار ہو گئے۔

stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot Secures First Coalition Pact in Effort to Form Israeli Government
stories.summary:
Israel’s Yashar party, headed by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, announced a coalition agreement with the right-wing opposition faction Israel Our Home, led by Avigdor Lieberman. The pact marks the first formal alliance since last month’s national election, which left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu without a parliamentary majority and created a political stalemate. President Isaac Herzog subsequently assigned Eisenkot the task of assembling a new governing administration within a 28-day mandate ending on December 6, while Netanyahu continues to serve in a caretaker capacity.

Prime Minister Netanyahu’s Likud party, together with its far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies, holds 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, falling short of a governing majority. Conversely, Eisenkot’s center-right Yashar faction and its patchwork partners command 48 seats. Although the newly formed agreement between Eisenkot and Lieberman brings together parties that previously expressed reservations about certain alliances, they share a unified objective to replace Netanyahu. Additionally, both factions could potentially find common ground with parties representing Israel's Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and strongly oppose the current caretaker prime minister.

Political negotiations remain fluid as discussions also continue regarding a potential unity government involving Likud, Eisenkot, and other change bloc partners. Complicating these efforts, the left-wing Democrats party suspended its talks with Eisenkot due to perceived progress in his parallel negotiations with Likud and ongoing deadlocks in forming an alternative government. If Eisenkot fails to build a viable coalition before his deadline expires or after requesting a standard extension, the mandate could shift to Netanyahu, with the alternative of fresh elections next year if all coalition efforts fail.

stories.title: NDMA Warns of Severe Smog and Hazardous Air Quality Across Punjab
stories.summary: The National Disaster Management Authority's National Emergencies Operations Centre issued a formal advisory warning residents about intensifying smog and dense fog expected to impact multiple districts in Punjab over a two-day period. According to the alert, toxic haze and severe atmospheric conditions are forecast to hit Lahore, Kasur, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Nankana Sahib, Sargodha, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Narowal, Okara, and Faisalabad, alongside southern and central sectors including Jhang, Khanewal, Multan, Khanpur, Kot Addu, and Bahawalpur. This heavy pollution significantly impairs visibility on local roads and major highways, creating hazardous traffic disruptions during early morning and late night periods. The NDMA urged travelers to exercise extreme caution during these hours and advised the public regarding severe health risks associated with prolonged exposure to polluted air. Medical experts recommend that children, elderly residents, and individuals suffering from pre-existing respiratory illnesses should take special precautions, wear protective masks outdoors, and limit outside exposure. In a related environmental development, Karachi recorded an Air Quality Index reading of 236 on Wednesday, categorizing its air as very unhealthy and positioning the port city as the second most polluted globally according to a global environmental monitoring report cited by ARY News.

stories.title: Chicago Soybean Futures Decline as Rapid Brazilian Planting Boosts Supply
stories.summary: Chicago soybean futures dropped on Wednesday, breaking a four-session winning streak as swift planting progress in Brazil raised expectations for global supplies early next year. Wheat prices also experienced a decline for the second consecutive session, while corn prices remained relatively flat amid shifting market dynamics. Traders in Singapore noted that prices are likely to face downward pressure unless unforeseen problems emerge within the South American crop. Agribusiness consultancy AgRural reported that Brazilian farmers had successfully planted 86 percent of the projected area for their 2026-27 soybean crop by the previous Thursday, increasing from 78 percent the prior week and exceeding the 81 percent completion rate recorded during the same period last year. Consequently, the most-active soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade lost 0.7 percent, settling at $12.25-1/2 a bushel by 0351 GMT. Meanwhile, wheat fell 0.5 percent to $5.86-1/2 a bushel, and corn held steady at $4.50-1/4 a bushel. Earlier support for the soybean market stemmed from strong demand for US soymeal, potentially driven by upcoming European Union deforestation rules, though a postponement of those regulations remains possible. Additionally, the US Department of Agriculture stated that 54 percent of the domestic winter wheat crop was rated in good-to-excellent condition, up slightly from 53 percent the previous week, while Russian wheat export prices rose following a trilateral presidential summit in Shenzhen, China.

stories.title: Rana Sanaullah Rejects Claims That Maryam Nawaz Will Replace Party President
stories.summary: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs Senator Rana Sanaullah Khan has dismissed speculation that Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif might succeed her father, Nawaz Sharif, as president of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N). During a television appearance, Sanaullah stated that she would never entertain such a concept in the presence of Nawaz Sharif, noting that she would expel any supporter who proposed it. He further remarked that Nawaz Sharif himself would not be permitted to step down even if he wished to do so. Commenting on the former prime minister's physical condition following a recent trip to Neelum Valley in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Sanaullah observed that Nawaz Sharif's health has significantly improved over the past five months and is much better than it was at any point over the previous five years. Comparing him to global leaders, Sanaullah noted that if US President Donald Trump could run for office at age 83, the 75-year-old Nawaz Sharif could continue leading the party for another five years. Addressing the contentious public debate regarding the creation of new provinces, Sanaullah explained that the PML-N is intentionally avoiding public commentary to prevent escalating tensions, emphasizing that any administrative division must be built on a solid consensus among all stakeholders before a potential referendum could be considered. These remarks followed political commentary suggesting an internal succession push within the ruling party for the upcoming 2029 general elections, as well as separate regional tensions surrounding the political status of Sindh. Meanwhile, Karachi was reported as the second most polluted city globally after its Air Quality Index reached 236.

stories.title: Chinese Yuan Reaches Three-Week High While Trade Tension Concerns Limit Gains
stories.summary: The Chinese yuan briefly reached its strongest level against the US dollar in more than three weeks during Wednesday trading, supported by a weakening greenback and consistent seasonal demand from corporate clients converting foreign currency. However, newly emerging trade tensions between the world's leading economies restricted further appreciation of the currency. Market analysts noted that trade policies drew renewed focus as the administration in Washington prepared to release findings from an investigation targeting perceived excess industrial capacity among trading partners like China and the European Union, echoing earlier tariff disputes from early 2025. Onshore yuan peaked at 6.6581 per dollar on Wednesday, marking its highest value since November 2, and traded marginally higher at 6.6659 by 0305 GMT, while the offshore rate hovered near 6.6557. Prior to market opening, the People's Bank of China established its official midpoint rate at 6.7088 per dollar, which represented its strongest fixing since July 2022, though it deviated significantly below market projections to carefully manage the velocity of currency appreciation. Additional support for the yuan continued to originate from corporate foreign exchange settlements, particularly exporters executing typical end-of-year conversions to fulfill administrative obligations, manage accounting requirements, and disburse holiday bonuses ahead of the Lunar New Year. Concurrently, the US dollar consolidated ahead of crucial inflation and growth reports ahead of a Federal Reserve policy meeting where market participants anticipate an interest rate hike.

stories.title: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari Rejects Imposed Orders and Affirms 1973 Constitution
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari stated that executive orders cannot impose constitutional amendments, referendums, or new provinces in the country. Speaking at a workers’ convention in Multan, he declared that the 1973 Constitution provides the sole framework for any national reset and warned against actions threatening political anarchy. 

Addressing the formation of new administrative regions, Bilawal emphasized that the establishment of separate provinces must follow the specific procedures outlined within the Constitution. He noted that while the Punjab Assembly unanimously passed a resolution supporting a Seraiki province through proper parliamentary steps, public representatives and the assembly in Sindh firmly rejected the division of their province. 

In addition to political remarks, environmental concerns drew attention as Karachi's Air Quality Index reached 236. According to global environmental monitors, the severe reading placed the city as the second most polluted globally, categorized strictly within the very unhealthy range. 

Bilawal concluded his address by withholding certain comments, promising to reveal further insights during an upcoming press meeting in Multan. His remarks underline ongoing debates regarding constitutional adherence, provincial boundaries, and environmental crises facing urban centers in Pakistan.

stories.title: London Copper Steadies Following Brief AI Rally and Tariff Pressures
stories.summary:
Benchmark copper prices in London stabilized following a severe overnight selloff that erased gains from a short-lived, artificial intelligence-driven relief rally. On the London Metal Exchange, three-month copper rose by 0.52 percent to reach $11,887.50 per metric ton, recovering slightly after hitting its lowest value since March 23. Concurrently, the most active January copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange dropped 4.66 percent to 89,520 yuan, equivalent to $13,433.37 per ton. 

The initial market surge occurred after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, boosting AI-related financial assets. However, optimism faded quickly as Nvidia shares dropped 5.9 percent and Asian stock markets tumbled amid broader technology sector volatility. Brokerage firm Everbright Futures noted that investors rapidly digested the leadership news before panic set in over fluctuating US technology stocks and potential inventory outflows. 

Adding to market pressure, the Trump administration prepared to release investigation findings regarding industrial overcapacity across 16 trading partners, including China and the European Union, signaling impending import tariffs. Other base metals experienced mixed results on the London Metal Exchange, where aluminum dipped to a 13-month low before temporary rule adjustments eased supply squeezes, while zinc, nickel, and lead saw modest gains.

stories.title: Chinese Equities Decline Amid Technology Losses and Trade Anxieties
stories.summary:
Chinese stock markets declined as regional indices followed overnight drops on Wall Street, with investors reacting to potential global trade conflicts. By midday, the benchmark Shanghai Composite and the blue-chip CSI300 index each fell by 1 percent. Technology shares experienced the steepest drops, mirroring a fading artificial intelligence rally after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive officer.

Semiconductor equities suffered heavily, pulling a specialized industry sub-index down by 4.9 percent, while the ChiNext Composite and STAR50 tech boards fell 1.7 percent and 2.6 percent respectively. Market sentiment was further dampened by expectations that the Trump administration would soon publish a probe targeting industrial overcapacity across 16 major trading partners, including China and the European Union, likely resulting in fresh import duties.

Analysts noted that Washington's restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips are expected to create economic headwinds for China. In response to tighter technological limits and softer domestic consumption, Nomura reduced its fourth-quarter gross domestic product growth forecast for China to 4.4 percent year-on-year and lowered its full-year 2026 outlook to 4.5 percent.

Across the wider Asia-Pacific region, MSCI's broadest index outside Japan dropped 2.5 percent. South Korean shares suffered a steep decline of up to 5.3 percent, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 2.9 percent, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index managed a modest gain of 0.2 percent.

stories.title: Bangladesh Garment Workers Secure Wage Increase After Weeks of Unrest
stories.summary:
Garment workers in Bangladesh secured a 36 percent increase in their minimum monthly wage following lengthy negotiations and weeks of sometimes violent protests. The protests had previously caused hundreds of millions of dollars in economic losses and disrupted shipments ahead of the crucial Christmas shopping season. The newly agreed minimum wage of 17,000 taka, supported by the majority of a government-appointed wage board, is scheduled to take effect in January.

The South Asian nation operates as the world's second-largest apparel exporter behind China, generating roughly four-fifths of its export earnings from a garment industry that employs more than four million people across some 4,000 factories. Workers initially demanded a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, up from the previous 12,500 taka, arguing that compensation failed to keep pace with soaring living expenses for food, housing, and healthcare. Although labor representatives expressed mixed feelings about the final figure, they urged employees to resume work.

Prior to the agreement, clashes broke out between police and demonstrators in industrial zones. The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association reported that recent disruptions cost the sector approximately $428 million, while orders valued at $254 million were diverted to other nations.

The garment sector remains Bangladesh's primary economic engine, supplying major global brands such as Levi Strauss and Fruit of the Loom across more than 150 countries. The United States remains its largest individual market, while the European Union serves as its biggest trading bloc, underscoring the vital global role played by the country's manufacturing workforce.

stories.title: بانی پی ٹی آئی اور بشریٰ بی بی کو فوری انصاف دیا جائے، بیرسٹر گوہر
stories.summary:
پاکستان تحریک انصاف کے چیئرمین بیرسٹر گوہر نے ایک بار پھر اعلیٰ عدلیہ سے اپیل کی ہے کہ بانی پی ٹی آئی اور بشریٰ بی بی کو فوری طور پر انصاف فراہم کیا جائے۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ بانی پی ٹی آئی نے دس روز قبل ملک کے تینوں چیف جسٹس صاحبان کو خط لکھ کر انصاف کی باقاعدہ اپیل کی تھی، مگر اس خط پر تحال کوئی کارروائی عمل میں نہیں لائی گئی۔

بیرسٹر گوہر نے اپنے بیان میں دہرایا کہ وہ آج مؤدبانہ گزارش کرتے ہیں کہ تینوں چیف جسٹس صاحبان بانی پی ٹی آئی اور بشریٰ بی بی کے معاملے میں تاخیر سے کام نہ لیں۔ یاد رہے کہ کچھ روز قبل بانی پی ٹی آئی عمران خان نے چیف جسٹس آف پاکستان، چیف جسٹس وفاقی آئینی عدالت اور چیف جسٹس اسلام آباد ہائیکورٹ کو خط ارسال کیا تھا جو ان کے وکیل بیرسٹر سلمان صفدر کے ذریعے پہنچایا گیا تھا۔

وکیل سلمان صفدر نے اس امر کی تصدیق کی تھی کہ یہ خط بانی پی ٹی آئی کی خصوصی ہدایت پر تحریر کیا گیا تھا۔ اس خط میں بنیادی طور پر بانی پی ٹی آئی کو فراہم کی جانے والی طبی سہولتوں اور عدالتوں کے احکامات پر ہوٹل اور دیگر مقامات پر عملدرآمد کرانے کی پُرزور اپیل کی گئی تھی۔

خط کے متن کے مطابق ڈاکٹروں نے خبردار کیا تھا کہ بانی پی ٹی آئی کو برین ہیمرج اور دل کا دورہ پڑنے کا شدید خطرہ لاحق ہو سکتا ہے کیونکہ ان کا بلڈ پریشر خطرناک حد تک بڑھ کر 193 تک پہنچ چکا ہے۔ اسی تشویشناک طبی صورتحال کے پیش نظر ان کے لیے فوری قانونی اور طبی اقدامات کا مطالبہ کیا جا رہا ہے۔

stories.title: پاکستان اور چین کا توانائی منصوبوں پر عملدرآمد اور مشترکہ تجارتی ٹیم تشکیل دینے کا فیصلہ
stories.summary:
وزیرِ پیٹرولیم علی پرویز ملک سے چینی سفیر جیانگ زیڈونگ نے ملاقات کی ہے جس میں دونوں ممالک نے ایل پی جی پلانٹ سمیت مختلف توانائی کے اہم منصوبوں پر جلد عمل درآمد کرنے پر اتفاق کیا ہے۔ اس ملاقات کے دوران پاکستان میں چینی سرمایہ کاری کے فروغ کے لیے ایک مشترکہ کمرشل یا تجارتی ٹیم تشکیل دینے کا بھی فیصلہ کیا گیا۔

اس ملاقات کے موقع پر پیٹرول کی درآمد، اس کے ذخیرہ کرنے اور ترسیل کے تمام انتظامات میں باہمی تعاون کو مزید بڑھانے پر بھی غور کیا گیا۔ وزیرِ پیٹرولیم علی پرویز ملک نے اس بات کا اعادہ کیا کہ پاکستان اور چین کے درمیان ہونے والی بات چیت کو عملی منصوبوں اور حقیقی صنعتی ترقی میں تبدیل کرنا ان کی اولین ترجیح ہے۔

علی پرویز ملک نے مزید کہا کہ چینی صدر کی ترجیحات دونوں دوست ممالک کے درمیان پاک چین توانائی شراکت داری کے مشترکہ وژن کی بھرپور عکاسی کرتی ہیں۔ انہوں نے پاکستانی ہیرو محمد ذیشان کی کامیابی پر پوری قوم کی طرف سے فخر کا اظہار بھی کیا۔

دوسری جانب چینی سفیر نے پاکستان کے ساتھ اپنا تعاون کا سلسلہ جاری رکھنے اور ملک میں سرمایہ کاری کے نئے اور بہتر مواقع تلاش کرنے کے عزم کا اعادہ کیا۔ ملاقات میں دونوں ملکوں کے درمیان آزاد تجارتی معاہدوں اور تعلقات کو مزید مستحکم کرنے پر بھی تبادلہ خیال کیا گیا۔

stories.title: خلائی سفر پر روانہ ہونے والے محمد ذیشان علی کو مسلح افواج کا خراج تحسین
stories.summary:
پاکستانی خلاباز محمد ذیشان علی کے تاریخی خلائی سفر پر ملک کی مسلح افواج نے اس سائنسی مشن میں شامل تمام سائنسدانوں، انجینئرز اور سپارکو کو زبردست خراج تحسین پیش کیا ہے۔ پاک فوج کے شعبہ تعلقات عامہ آئی ایس پی آر کی جانب سے جاری کردہ بیان میں کہا گیا ہے کہ یہ خلائی مشن ملکی سائنسی اور تکنیکی ترقی کے سفر میں ایک سنگ میل کی حیثیت رکھتا ہے۔

مسلح افواج نے اس تاریخی مشن کی کامیابی میں بھرپور تعاون کرنے پر چین کی قیادت، حکومت اور وہاں کے عوام کا خصوصی شکریہ ادا کیا۔ بیان میں کہا گیا ہے کہ پاک چین دوستی اب زمین کی محدود سرحدوں سے بھی آگے نکل کر خلا کی لامحدود وسعتوں تک جا پہنچی ہے۔

محمد ذیشان علی چین کے تیان گونگ خلائی اسٹیشن پر قدم رکھنے والے پہلے غیر ملکی خلا باز بن گئے ہیں، جنہوں نے صبح پانچ بج کر اٹھارہ منٹ پر خلا کی جانب تاریخی پرواز کی۔ اس موقع پر فیلڈ مارشل سید عاصم منیر سمیت تمام سروسز چیفس نے پوری قوم، سپارکو اور سائنسی کمیونٹی کو اس شاندار کامیابی پر مبارکباد دی۔

حکومت کے دیگر رہنماؤں بشمول احسن اقبال اور آصف علی زرداری نے بھی اس امر پر فخر کا اظہار کیا کہ پاکستان نے انسانی خلائی پرواز میں شرکت کر کے تاریخ رقم کی ہے اور یہ قوم کے لیے ایک عظیم اور فخر کا لمحہ ہے۔ چینی سفارت خانے نے بھی اس موقع پر پاک چین دوستی کے پیغام پر مبنی ایک مختصر ویڈیو جاری کی۔

stories.title: Two Libyan Soldiers Die From Injuries Following Attack on Russian Ships
stories.summary:
Two soldiers from Libya's naval forces succumbed to injuries they sustained in an attack on Russian vessels near Benghazi, according to a senior official in the eastern administration. The military strike, which targeted the Benghazi Naval Base and involved seven Ukrainian-made naval drones, was claimed by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to sink a Russian naval corvette and cargo ship.

Libya remains politically divided between a UN-recognized government based in Tripoli and a parallel administration in the east that is supported by military commander Khalifa Haftar and maintains strong ties with Russia. Saddam Haftar, a prominent figure in the eastern military camp, paid tribute to the two deceased soldiers on Facebook, while eastern government head Oussama Hamad condemned what he described as treacherous Ukrainian aggression.

The incident has heightened concerns about an escalation of the crisis in the divided North African nation. In response to the attack, the eastern administration requested that the United Nations investigate the alleged presence of Ukrainian forces in western Libya. Furthermore, eastern authorities announced plans to launch a joint investigation alongside Russia into the strikes on the vessels.

stories.title: Asian and Wall Street Tech Shares Plunge as Nvidia Rally Fades
stories.summary:
