Technology stocks across Asia and Wall Street suffered sharp declines on Wednesday as renewed anxiety surrounding the artificial intelligence sector quickly overshadowed the recent market euphoria. The downturn followed a brief market boost driven by the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia less than two weeks after his resignation over extramarital affairs. Despite the relief surrounding Huang's return, analysts emphasized persistent investor worries regarding the enormous capital expenditures poured into artificial intelligence and the uncertainty of future returns.

Asian stock markets experienced significant losses, reversing explosive gains from the previous session. Major regional technology hubs saw steep drops, with Taipei plunging eight percent, Seoul falling over five percent, and Tokyo dropping more than three percent. Heavy selling impacted leading chip manufacturers such as Taiwan's TSMC and MediaTek, Japan's Kioxia and Advantest, and South Korean giants SK hynix and Samsung, alongside widespread declines in Shanghai, Sydney, and Singapore.

Wall Street mirrored the downward trend as Nvidia shares fell nearly six percent following a 31 percent surge, while AI rival Anthropic dropped below its initial public offering price. Major indices such as the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 both retreated as professional investors reportedly used the rebound to reduce technology exposure. Market participants are now shifting their attention to upcoming inflation data and potential Federal Reserve interest rate decisions.

stories.title: Thieves Steal 49,000 Litres of Fuel From PSO Pipeline in Islamabad
stories.summary:
Thieves stole 49,000 litres of diesel valued at Rs17.6 million from a main Pakistan State Oil (PSO) pipeline in a rural area of Islamabad. The theft, which began on October 16, was uncovered after officials at the PSO Sihala Terminal noticed a continuous drop in pipeline pressure during specific daily hours and initiated strict surveillance operations.

Following a formal complaint filed by PSO official Mohammad Rahmet Ullah, local police registered a case under the Pakistan Penal Code provisions related to petroleum pipeline tampering. PSO security guards patrolling the 15-kilometre pipeline observed suspicious activity involving a tank-equipped truck at a Model Town residence on November 23. Law enforcement and security personnel subsequently searched the premises, where they discovered vehicles, a high-pressure pipe, and a nozzle inside a pit beneath a kitchen floor slab.

Further inspection revealed a tunnel connected directly to the primary PSO pipeline running alongside the property wall. During the investigation, a suspect at the house admitted to colluding with accomplices in petroleum theft from multiple locations. This incident follows similar past occurrences, including the theft of over Rs80 million worth of diesel in October 2024 and a Federal Investigation Agency operation in July 2026 that dismantled a network illegally extracting fuel near Sihala.

stories.title: Zeeshan Ali Becomes First Pakistani Astronaut in Historic Space Mission
stories.summary:
Pakistani astronaut Zeeshan Ali became the first citizen of his country to enter orbit after China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre. The spacecraft, powered by a Long March 2-F rocket, blasted off and docked with China's Tiangong space station roughly three hours and 38 minutes later, making Ali the first foreign national to board the self-built orbital facility.

Ali is serving as a payload specialist alongside Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and mission pilot Wu Yi. During his roughly one-week stay in space, Ali will conduct approximately 90 experiments alongside the Chinese crew, including cultivating microalgae as a potential oxygen and food source for future missions and testing spaceflight effects on quinoa seeds. The mission follows a bilateral space cooperation agreement signed between Pakistan's space agency Suparco and the China Manned Space Agency in February 2025.

 Pakistani leaders, including Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, hailed the launch as a monumental milestone for the nation's space ambitions and technological progress. In his pre-launch remarks, the 40-year-old astronaut expressed deep gratitude to the Chinese government and emphasized that the flight serves as a launch pad for future bilateral space cooperation involving missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

stories.title: Peshawar Administration Announces Crackdown on Unregistered Rickshaws
stories.summary:
The Peshawar administration is preparing to execute a major operation against illegally operating rickshaws in the city to address growing traffic congestion. Peshawar Commissioner Khalid Mahmood stated that over 100,000 rickshaws currently operate in the urban area, while only 25,000 have been issued valid route permits. The local administration aims to identify unauthorized vehicles, regulate their movement, and formulate new regulations for legally registered transport.

Under the proposed measures, authorities intend to restrict rickshaw movement on major roads and Bus Rapid Transit routes. The city administration is also considering the implementation of designated routes and specific operating hours for these vehicles. These steps are designed to reduce traffic bottlenecks, organize the local transport network, and ensure strict compliance with existing transport laws.

This initiative follows a similar crackdown launched by the Islamabad Traffic Police against loaders, Chingchi rickshaws, and passenger rickshaws entering the federal capital. Chief Traffic Officer Kainat Azhar Khan visited checkpoints during the operation to brief officers on enforcing restrictions. Islamabad police officials were instructed to take strict action against traffic violations to facilitate commuters and improve traffic flow.

Growth in the number of unregulated vehicles has heightened concerns among municipal authorities in both cities. By addressing these violations, the Peshawar administration hopes to establish a more orderly transport system. The ongoing efforts highlight a broader regional push by traffic police and commissioners to curb unauthorized transit operations and ease daily congestion.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Gains as Asian Markets Decline on Tariffs
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange opened on a positive note, with buying interest keeping the benchmark KSE-100 index in the green during morning trading on Wednesday. By 9:45 am, the index hovered at 178,860.15 points, marking an increase of 317.87 points or 0.18 percent. Positive sentiment was noted across several key sectors, including automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies, oil marketing companies, and refineries.

Index-heavy equities such as ARL, HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, HBL, MEBL, MCB, and UBL traded upward. This followed a broad-based rally on Tuesday when the KSE-100 index climbed 1,068.42 points, or 0.60 percent, to close at 178,542.28 points, supported by declining international oil prices that improved investor sentiment.

In contrast, Asian stock markets tumbled early Wednesday due to fresh United States tariff threats and a fading tech-led rally. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 2.3 percent, driven by sharp declines in South Korea and Taiwan. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell by up to 2.9 percent. Risk appetite weakened following reports that the Trump administration was preparing trade investigation findings that could introduce new tariff measures.

Wall Street stocks finished mixed overnight, with the S&P 500 down 0.5 percent and the Nasdaq Composite lower by 1.5 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.9 percent. Market attention has now shifted toward upcoming US core PCE data ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Meanwhile, individual stocks such as Nvidia fell 5.9 percent following Jensen Huang's return as CEO, and Anthropic dropped 6.5 percent below its IPO price.

stories.title: China Docking Shenzhou-24 Brings Pakistan’s First Astronaut to Space
stories.summary:
China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully docked with the Tiangong space station three hours and 38 minutes after liftoff, according to the China Manned Space Agency. A Long March 2-F rocket carried the mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 8:18 am Beijing time. The crew consists of Chinese commander Tang Hongbo, pilot Wu Yi, and 40-year-old payload specialist Zeeshan Ali, who made history as Pakistan's first astronaut in orbit and the first foreign national to board the Tiangong station.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal attended the send-off ceremony in China and hailed the event as a monumental milestone for bilateral friendship and Pakistan's space aspirations. Pakistan’s space agency, SUPARCO, and the CMSA previously signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025 to train Pakistani astronauts. Ali arrived at the Astronaut Centre of China months prior for specialized preparation alongside his colleagues.

During his weeklong stay aboard the station, Ali will participate in scientific investigations alongside the Chinese crew. SUPARCO confirmed his tasks will include cultivating microalgae as a future oxygen and food source, and testing spaceflight impacts on quinoa seeds. The broader mission involves roughly 90 total experiments, routine station maintenance, and an orbital crew rotation with members of the preceding Shenzhou-23 mission.

Beijing has invested heavily in its space program with the goal of landing astronauts on the Moon before 2030. Meanwhile, departing Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu will remain on the station for a year to study human adaptation in space, setting a record for the longest single orbital stay by a Chinese astronaut. The collaborative mission represents a significant leap forward for Pakistan-China technological cooperation.

stories.title: OICCI Survey Shows Sharp Decline in Pakistan Business Confidence
stories.summary:
Business confidence in Pakistan has deteriorated sharply despite a recent increase in foreign direct investment, according to the latest Business Confidence Survey released by the Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry. Conducted nationwide between September and October, the Wave 30 survey revealed that overall business confidence plunged by 36 percentage points, falling from a positive 13 percent to a negative 23 percent. Sentiment among OICCI member foreign investors dropped even more dramatically by 55 percentage points, moving from positive 28 percent to negative 27 percent.

The findings carry significant weight as the survey represents businesses generating nearly 80 percent of Pakistan’s GDP across manufacturing, services, and retail sectors in metro and non-metro areas. The decline in morale stems from mounting economic pressures, including high energy and fuel prices, persistent inflation, geopolitical tensions, security concerns, and policy uncertainty. Conversely, State Bank data indicated that foreign direct investment rose by 22 percent during the first four months of fiscal year 2027, reaching $935 million compared to $764 million during the same period in the previous year.

Confidence turned negative across all three major sectors surveyed. Retail and wholesale experienced the steepest drop, plunging 45 percentage points to negative 25 percent, while manufacturing fell 34 points to negative 25 percent and services dropped 31 points to negative 17 percent. Capital investment expectations decreased by 16 percentage points, and employment expectations fell by 23 points. Furthermore, 78 percent of respondents reported a negative assessment of the business environment over the preceding six months.

OICCI President Umar Ahsan Khan emphasized that policymakers must address underlying structural issues to achieve sustainable economic growth driven by the private sector. He noted that businesses require a predictable policy environment, competitive taxation, and reliable energy supplies to unlock fresh investments. OICCI Secretary General M. Abdul Aleem expressed surprise at the extent of disappointment among established foreign investors, who historically maintained higher confidence levels than the broader business community.

stories.title: US Jury Convicts Huawei of Trade Secret Theft and Fraud
stories.summary:
A federal jury in New York has found the Chinese technology company Huawei guilty on 10 out of 12 criminal charges following a three-month trial. The verdict includes convictions for bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, and conspiracy to steal trade secrets over business dealings related to Iran. Prosecutors stated that the telecommunications manufacturer lied about its activities in Iran to gain billions of dollars and access to US-dollar clearing services, while also attempting to recruit US tech employees to obtain proprietary data.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche emphasized that no entity is above the law, noting that Huawei and its subsidiaries operated using falsehoods and theft. Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva added that the outcome demonstrates America's commitment to protecting its businesses, workers, and national security from foreign corporations that use illicit methods to gain advantages.

Despite the major convictions, the jury acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. A company spokesperson welcomed the acquittals, asserting that they confirm the lack of factual basis for those specific allegations while vowing to review the remaining verdicts and pursue legal actions to defend its rights.

For years, Huawei has faced heavy scrutiny from US administrations over espionage risks, leading Washington to discourage nations from using its infrastructure for 5G networks. The company maintains that the convictions lack both legal and factual merit as the legal battle continues.

stories.title: England Level T20 Series Against Australia With Comfortable Win
stories.summary:
England secured an eight-wicket victory against Australia on Tuesday in Gold Coast, leveling the Twenty20 international series at 1-1. Chasing a target of 185, openers Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt established a dominant 151-run partnership that dismantled the Australian bowling attack from the beginning.

Donald played a stellar innings, smashing 85 runs from 32 deliveries with nine sixes and four fours before being dismissed by Riley Meredith. Salt contributed 58 runs off 30 balls, featuring four sixes and five fours, before falling to a remarkable one-handed catch-and-bowled dismissal by Ben Dwarshuis. Captain Harry Brook and Tom Banton then comfortably sealed the victory, reaching 188-2 in 13.1 overs with 41 balls remaining.

Earlier in the match, Australia chose to bat first after winning the previous series opener. However, regular wickets fell, with Henry Crocombe and Sam Curran each claiming two wickets as Australia stumbled to 84-5 after 11 overs. A recovery was led by Nikhil Chaudhary, who scored 45 runs, and Joel Davies, who added 39 runs. Dwarshuis provided late momentum by hitting three consecutive sixes off Curran to bring the total to 184-8.

Australian captain Mitchell Marsh acknowledged the strong performance by the visiting openers, noting that the surface improved later in the game. England captain Brook praised the explosive opening partnership as an absolute clinic that put on an impressive display.

stories.title: Ben Stokes Registers for 2027 IPL Auction With BCCI Permission
stories.summary:
Former England cricket captain Ben Stokes has officially registered for the upcoming Indian Premier League mini-player auction. The 35-year-old all-rounder is set to enter the auction pool scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16.

Under standard tournament regulations, players who skip the major mega auction are generally barred from participating in the subsequent mini auction, which would normally have kept Stokes out of the pool until 2027. However, Indian media reports indicate that the Board of Control for Cricket in India has granted Stokes special permission to enter this year's auction despite the rule.

Stokes, who announced his retirement from international cricket earlier this year, previously played for the Chennai Super Kings in 2023. Over the course of five seasons in the league, he has accumulated 935 runs and taken 28 wickets across 45 matches.

stories.title: Australia and Solomon Islands Sign New Defense and Security Pact
stories.summary:
Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a bilateral security pact on Wednesday, establishing Canberra as the Pacific archipelago's primary defense partner. The agreement expands Australian involvement in local police and border forces and mandates that Honiara consult with Australia regarding critical infrastructure development.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated during a press conference with Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale that taking on the role of main security partner is a serious responsibility. The deal represents a significant diplomatic victory for Canberra amid ongoing competition with China for regional influence, following similar agreements signed with Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, and Fiji.

The pact also marks a notable shift for Wale, a long-standing critic of China who previously voiced strong opposition to a 2022 security deal between Honiara and Beijing. Although Wale led a delegation to Beijing in 2025 and praised its economic development, Australian media reported on Wednesday that the prior arrangement with China has now been scrapped, though Wale declined to comment directly due to a non-disclosure agreement.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs Predicts Surging US Data Center Power and Gas Demand
stories.summary:
Goldman Sachs released a note on Tuesday stating that rapid power capacity growth in United States data centers will likely persist through 2028. This expansion is heavily fueled by the artificial intelligence boom, which is encouraging the creation of more, larger, and increasingly power-dense facilities across the country. According to the brokerage, data-center power capacity and demand have jumped by nearly 30 percent year-to-date in the US, accounting for more than one-third of total power demand growth.

This continuous expansion poses upside risks to power and natural gas markets, tightening the domestic power sector and driving up natural gas consumption. Consequently, the trend reinforces Goldman's bullish outlook for Henry Hub gas prices covering the period from 2028 to 2030. The firm noted that the growth acceleration will stem not only from a higher volume of operational facilities, but also from expansive physical footprints and higher power density requirements.

Despite this strong outlook, the brokerage warned that potential policy shifts following midterm elections could temper these upside risks. In particular, Democratic victories in November, which included key wins in Republican strongholds and major data center hubs like Texas and Georgia, are expected to establish a divided government. This political shift could subsequently introduce greater regulatory scrutiny into future data center developments nationwide.

Understanding these market dynamics matters because the unprecedented energy demands of artificial intelligence infrastructure directly threaten to strain regional power grids and shift commodity pricing. By highlighting how technological growth intersects with utility markets and legislative changes, the findings provide crucial insight for energy investors, policymakers, and utility providers managing the looming resource crunch through the end of the decade.

stories.title: Starbucks Taps Banks to Explore Sale of Japan Operations
stories.summary:
Global coffee giant Starbucks has reportedly initiated preparations for a potential sale of its Japanese business unit, which is valued at several billion dollars. According to a Bloomberg News report on Tuesday, the company has enlisted major financial institutions, including Citigroup and Morgan Stanley, to act as advisers for the transaction. People familiar with the matter indicated that initial discussions have already begun to gauge the interest of various strategic and financial investors.

The development follows earlier reporting by Reuters in September, which revealed that Starbucks was actively evaluating the divestment of a majority stake in its Japanese enterprise. That potential deal could value the company-operated entity—representing its largest overseas market—at approximately $3 billion. However, Reuters was unable to immediately verify the latest Bloomberg report regarding the formalized banking engagements.

The prospective sale represents a major strategic maneuver for Starbucks regarding its international corporate structure and asset portfolio. Because Japan houses the coffee chain's biggest overseas company-operated market, any alterations to ownership could reshape its regional retail footprint and capital allocation strategies. Market observers and investors are closely monitoring the situation as the firm works alongside financial advisers to navigate the potential multi-billion-dollar transaction.

stories.title: Zeeshan Ali becomes first Pakistani astronaut on China mission
stories.summary:
Pakistani and Chinese astronauts launched into space aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, creating a historic milestone for Pakistan. Zeeshan Ali became the first Pakistani citizen to travel into space and the initial foreign astronaut to enter China’s Tiangong Space Station. Accompanied by two Chinese crewmates, Ali departed from a Chinese launch center at 5:18 a.m. Pakistan Standard Time.

The space crew will remain in orbit for one week to perform approximately 90 scientific experiments and technology tests, including four specific Pakistani university proposals focused on agriculture, food security, vacuum science, and materials science. SUPARCO Chairman Muhammad Yousuf Khan noted that 19 candidates were tested in China before Ali and his backup were chosen for seven months of rigorous training.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal praised the launch as a historic achievement reflecting the strong bilateral ties between Pakistan and China. SUPARCO highlighted the country's recent space progress, which includes launching six satellites in thirty months and aiming for a future lunar landing.

The spacecraft was carried into orbit by a rocket, separating at an approximate altitude of 400 kilometers to continue toward the space station. Officials emphasized that the mission's findings will be shared with Pakistan to aid technological advancements across various domestic sectors.

stories.title: Senator Sherry Rehman warns of systemic violence against women
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman warned that gender-based violence in the nation represents a systemic crisis rather than a private matter. Speaking on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, she highlighted severe shortcomings in protection frameworks, reporting mechanisms, and judicial administration.

Rehman shared figures indicating that Pakistan recorded 32,617 cases of gender-based violence in 2024, which included domestic abuse, kidnapping, rape, and honour killings. These numbers average out daily to 19 rapes, 67 kidnappings, six domestic violence incidents, and two honour killings. She further noted that conviction rates sit around 5 percent, while acquittals reach approximately 64 percent.

Citing the Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey, Rehman pointed out that 34 percent of ever-married women have experienced spousal violence within their homes and communities. She emphasized that fear, social stigma, family pressure, and widespread impunity prevent many victims from seeking assistance or speaking out.

Rehman called for accessible shelters, financial support, and legal aid to ensure women facing abusive situations have realistic options to leave. Her remarks underscored ongoing nationwide concerns regarding safety, trauma, and justice for vulnerable women and girls.

stories.title: Imran Khan directs PTI to expand political alliances
stories.summary:
The PTI core committee was instructed by its incarcerated founder, Imran Khan, to expand its political alliance by reaching out to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties to form a broader coalition. Lawyer Latif Khosa conveyed these directives after meeting Khan and Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail, while the PPP responded by urging the PTI to first demonstrate effectiveness as the main opposition inside and outside parliament.

During the meeting chaired by Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, the core committee also reviewed instructions regarding the creation of new provinces, which will be evaluated by the PTI parliamentary party. The committee expressed grave concern over Khan's health, demanding the implementation of a Supreme Court order to transfer him to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, and called for medical treatment orders for Bushra Bibi to be honored.

Additionally, the committee condemned the continued detention of lawmakers and officials, including Sohail Afridi, and urged the Federal Constitutional Court to modify stay orders concerning Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order. They also resolved to observe November 26 as "Martyrs' Day" to honor individuals killed during protests in 2024.

Meanwhile, PPP General Secretary Nayyer Hussain Bukhari stated that his party has not yet decided to leave the federal government. He criticized the PTI for failing to respond to an invitation to return to parliamentary standing committees and questioned the political agendas of both the PTI and PML-N regarding the creation of new administrative provinces.

stories.title: Malaysia Aviation Group orders ten Boeing 787 Dreamliners
stories.summary:
Malaysia Aviation Group, the parent company of Malaysia Airlines, announced plans to purchase 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners as part of an ongoing fleet modernisation initiative. MAG President and Chief Executive Officer Nasaruddin A Bakar stated that the order includes an option to acquire an additional six aircraft, though financial terms and delivery schedules were not immediately released.

Nasaruddin explained that the Dreamliners will provide the necessary capacity, flexibility, and efficiency to sustain the airline's long-term growth. This follows a previous agreement where Malaysia stated it would buy 30 Boeing 737 MAX narrowbody jets, with an option for 30 more, stemming from a trade deal between Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and US President Donald Trump.

To manage costs driven by higher jet fuel prices from Middle East conflicts, MAG reduced its capacity by roughly 6 percent, amounting to 8,000 to 9,000 flights, earlier in the year. However, the company aims to increase its capacity by approximately 8 percent in the upcoming year.

The announcement follows a recent deal by China Southern Airlines subsidiary Xiamen Airlines to purchase 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 planes, marking a significant US airplane transaction in the Chinese market.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Expected to Recover as Foreign Investors Return
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is anticipated to restart its upward movement on Wednesday. Market participants expect the currency to open between 92.70 and 92.75 against the dollar following a recent decline from a seven-month peak of 92.43 down to 92.91 on Monday. Indian financial markets remained closed on Tuesday for a holiday.

Monday's pullback ended a winning streak for the currency, driven by heavy corporate purchases of dollars and technical indicators showing the asset was heavily overbought. However, banking professionals characterized this dip as a standard and healthy correction instead of a permanent trend reversal. Analysts note that a significant escalation in oil prices or a sudden shift in overseas investments would be required to alter the positive underlying trajectory.

Foreign interest in Indian equities has revived, with overseas funds investing more than $14 billion during the month and pushing the rupee up by over two percent. This capital inflow occurred despite benchmark indices falling nearly two percent on Monday. Global concerns regarding artificial intelligence valuations and tech-led rallies are prompting international investors to reallocate funds toward Indian assets.

Fluctuations in technology stocks and the Nasdaq remain crucial factors influencing foreign capital flows into India. Market sensitivity regarding Nvidia and the actual financial returns on artificial intelligence investments continue to create volatility. Currency traders state that these technology sector swings will ultimately dictate the direction of foreign investments in local markets.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Result in Casualties and Property Damage in Ukraine
stories.summary:
A Russian attack in the Odesa region of Ukraine resulted in two fatalities and three injuries, including a child. According to regional governor Oleh Kiper, writing on Telegram late on Tuesday, the assault impacted private structures, industrial properties, and various vehicles along the Black Sea coast.

Concurrently, Russian forces targeted the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv with a barrage of drones late Tuesday evening. Vitali Klitschko, the mayor of Kyiv, stated on Telegram that falling drone debris sparked a blaze across the lower two floors of a 16-story apartment building situated in a central district of the city. Witnesses in the capital reported hearing multiple explosions during the assault.

Two residents sustained injuries during the drone attack on the apartment complex and received medical treatment directly at the scene. While these incidents add to the ongoing destruction, Reuters could not independently verify the details of the reports. Both governments involved in the conflict maintain that they do not deliberately target civilian populations.

These events underscore an ongoing pattern of violence, as Russian forces have subjected Kyiv and other urban centers across Ukraine to near-constant bombardment since September. The continuous drone and missile strikes continue to cause widespread damage to residential areas and critical infrastructure throughout the country.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis Issue Threats Against Saudi Red Sea Ports
stories.summary:
Yemen’s Houthi movement announced on Wednesday that Saudi Arabia’s port of Jeddah and all other Saudi ports situated along the Red Sea coast will become military targets. The warning was issued in response to perceived threats by Saudi Arabia to attack the Yemeni port of Hodeidah.

In an official statement delivered by spokesperson Yahya Saree, the group demanded that port employees, nearby workers, and local residents evacuate the facilities immediately. Furthermore, the Houthi leadership strongly advised all commercial shipping companies to withdraw their vessels from the threatened locations.

Shortly after the Houthi announcement, the Saudi-led military coalition launched retaliatory operations. The coalition confirmed in a Wednesday statement that it struck operational capabilities at Hodeidah and destroyed multiple targets located within the Yemeni governorates of Saada and Amran.

Tensions and hostilities between the two opposing sides have escalated significantly since September. The renewed violence intensified when Houthi forces advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital shipping chokepoint situated at the southern entry point of the Red Sea.

In the wake of these developments, the conflict has seen a reciprocal escalation in attacks. The Houthis have frequently targeted Saudi infrastructure including airports, ports, and oil facilities, while the Saudi-led coalition has intensified its aerial bombardment of Houthi positions inside Yemen.

stories.title: Gold Prices Dip While Investors Await Key US Inflation Data
stories.summary:
Gold prices moved lower on Wednesday, extending a more than two percent drop from the previous session. Spot gold decreased by 0.3 percent to reach $3,544.54 per ounce, while US gold futures for December fell 0.5 percent to $3,542.60. The downward pressure stems from hawkish communications by the US Federal Reserve, which have strengthened expectations for a December interest rate hike.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh recently highlighted artificial intelligence as a critical turning point for American economic leadership. However, the technology has also become a central debate for monetary policy officials trying to determine if the artificial intelligence boom acts as a driver of inflation, a transformational economic moment, or a precursor to a financial downturn. Meanwhile, US consumer confidence reached a nearly two-year high in November, fueled by optimism regarding labor markets and post-election economic conditions.

Market participants are now closely monitoring the upcoming US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Index, the central bank's favored inflation gauge, which targets a two percent annual rate. According to the CME FedWatch tool, financial markets are currently pricing in a 96.4 percent probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the upcoming December Fed meeting, alongside a 3.6 percent chance of a larger 50-basis-point adjustment. Higher interest rates typically raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, diminishing its attractiveness to investors.

In other precious metals markets, spot silver slipped 0.2 percent to $40.79 per ounce, platinum dropped 0.7 percent to $1,267.65, and palladium lost 0.3 percent, trading at $851.25 per ounce. Globally, central bank policies remain in focus, as former Bank of Japan policymaker Seiji Adachi noted that additional rate hikes are likely ahead, though weak consumption could pose political challenges next year.

stories.title: Asian Stocks Plunge Amid Renewed US Tariff Threats and Tech Slump
stories.summary:
Asian stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Wednesday, driven by fresh trade threats from the United States and a fading technology sector rally. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 2.3 percent, with South Korean and Taiwanese markets facing steep losses of up to 5.3 percent and 5.1 percent, respectively. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell as much as 2.9 percent, while S&P 500 e-mini futures decreased by 0.3 percent.

The market selloff occurred after reports emerged that the Trump administration is preparing to release a trade investigation regarding excess industrial capacity across 16 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. Analysts noted that investors are hesitant to commit significant capital amid these revived trade tensions and lingering concerns over the US debt ceiling. Meanwhile, Wall Street finished mixed in the previous session, with the S&P 500 losing 0.5 percent and the Nasdaq Composite dropping 1.5 percent.

In currency and commodity markets, the Australian dollar strengthened following higher-than-expected October consumer price data, which showed annualised trimmed mean inflation running at 3.8 percent. This persistent inflation places additional pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia, which has already raised interest rates by 125 basis points this year. Brent crude oil opened 0.5 percent lower at $90.97 in Asia following a volatile prior session.

Investors are now turning their attention toward upcoming US economic data, including core Personal Consumption Expenditures figures, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Market participants are carefully evaluating economic fundamentals following strong November consumer confidence numbers and positive earnings reports from Dell. Cryptocurrencies also drifted lower, with Bitcoin falling 1 percent to $59,257.71 and ether sliding 1.1 percent to $1,660.52.

stories.title: US Dollar Consolidates Ahead of Key Inflation and GDP Reports
stories.summary:
The US dollar paused its recent strong run on Wednesday as traders awaited crucial growth and inflation data ahead of the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting. Market participants are currently pricing in a 97 percent probability of a Fed interest rate hike. The dollar index remained flat at 103.85, following a 0.44 percent decline in the previous session.

Global currencies reacted to a mix of domestic economic updates and central bank policies. The Japanese yen held steady after figures showed October service-sector prices rose to a 36-year high, increasing by 4.2 percent year-over-year. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar climbed 0.29 percent to $0.6657 following higher-than-forecast consumer price inflation data that underlined the necessity of recent interest rate increases.

Later in the day, the US Commerce Department is expected to release the second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product, anticipated to show a 3.5 percent annualised growth rate. Additionally, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index is projected to edge up 0.3 percent for October, following a 0.5 percent gain the prior month. These figures will provide key insights into economic momentum and central bank policy paths.

Elevated oil prices, driven by the ongoing Middle East crisis, have maintained hawkish postures among central banks globally. European Central Bank policymaker Olaf Sleijpen indicated that the ECB is likely to raise its policy interest rate in December. In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin decreased by 0.52 percent to $59,507.77, and ether dipped 0.54 percent to $1,669.73.

stories.title: پہلا پاکستانی خلا باز محمد ذیشان علی چین کے شین ژو-24 مشن کے ساتھ خلا میں روانہ
stories.summary:
پاکستانی خلاباز محمد ذیشان علی چینی شین ژو-24 مشن کے ذریعے خلا میں روانہ ہو گئے ہیں اور وہ خلا کا سفر کرنے والے پہلے پاکستانی بن گئے ہیں۔ اس تاریخی سفر کے لیے محمد ذیشان علی اور خرم داؤد کو رواں سال اپریل میں چین میں خصوصی تربیت کے لیے منتخب کیا گیا تھا۔

محمد ذیشان علی چین کے تیانگونگ خلائی سٹیشن پر چھ روز قیام کے دوران بطور پے لوڈ سپیشلسٹ سائنسی تجربات میں حصہ لیں گے۔ وہ تیانگونگ خلائی سٹیشن تک پہنچنے والے پہلے غیر ملکی خلا باز بھی ہیں، اور یہ چین کے انسانی خلائی پروگرام کے تحت چینی اور غیر ملکی خلابازوں کی پہلی مشترکہ پرواز ہے۔

سپارکو اور چائنا مینڈ سپیس ایجنسی کے اشتراک سے ہونے والے ان تجربات کا تعلق میٹریل سائنس، فلوئیڈ فزکس، حیاتیاتی علوم اور بائیوٹیکنالوجی سے ہے۔ مشن کے دوران مائیکرو الجی کی افزائش، کوئنوا کے بیجوں پر کائناتی شعاعوں کے اثرات اور خود کو مرمت کرنے والے جدید مواد کا جائزہ لیا جائے گا۔

ماہرین کے مطابق ان تحقیقات سے موسمیاتی تبدیلیوں، غذائی تحفظ، مضبوط فصلوں کی تیاری اور صنعتی ترقی میں مدد ملے گی۔ انسٹی ٹیوٹ آف سپیس ٹیکنالوجی کے پروفیسر ڈاکٹر خرم خورشید اور پنجاب یونیورسٹی کے پروفیسر ڈاکٹر سید عامر محمود کا کہنا ہے کہ یہ مشن پاکستان کے طویل مدتی خلائی پروگرام کا اہم حصہ ہے۔

چین کے سرکاری ذرائع کے مطابق اس مشن میں تقریباً 90 سائنسی تجربات انجام دیے جائیں گے، اور مستقبل میں ایسے مزید مشنز کے لیے پاکستانی خلانوردوں کے تربیتی نصاب کو دیگر ممالک کے لیے بھی استعمال کیا جائے گا۔

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Conduct Violations at All-Hands Meeting
stories.summary:
Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addressed employees during an hour-long all-hands meeting at the company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, admitting to code of conduct violations and severe mistakes. Huang firmly denied reports that his reinstatement was the result of political pressure from US President Donald Trump on the board, stating he is currently in therapy and acknowledging that his previous actions were unacceptable.

Huang's return follows his resignation last week due to revelations of extramarital affairs, which briefly unsettled markets and the artificial intelligence ecosystem. Nvidia shares closed 5.9 percent lower as investors refocused on governance risks. Despite criticism from lawmakers regarding the circumstances of his return, Nvidia's board maintained that government input confirmed Huang poses no national security risk.

President Trump stated in interviews that he believes Nvidia's success is vital for American leadership in artificial intelligence and noted openness to exploring various governance arrangements, including potential equity stakes. Meanwhile, Huang and Nvidia face multiple state and federal investigations, including inquiries from the FBI, the Justice Department, and the Securities and Exchange Commission, alongside an upcoming public Senate hearing scheduled for December 3.

While Nvidia's initial market surge following Huang's reinstatement briefly propelled the company back into second place globally behind Apple, analysts remain cautious. Market observers emphasize that corporate governance concerns and upcoming regulatory scrutiny present ongoing risks for the chipmaker despite its strong financial position.

stories.title: Indian Shares Anticipate Positive Opening on Foreign Inflows and Easing Oil
stories.summary:
Indian stock markets are poised for a positive opening on Wednesday, aiming to recover some of the ground lost during the previous session. GIFT Nifty futures indicated a firm start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index, which closed at 25,349.65 on Monday before markets were closed on Tuesday for a local holiday. The expected rebound is supported by continued foreign investment and declining crude oil prices.

Foreign institutional investors remain net buyers in India, pumping in a record $14.28 billion so far this month amid a broader rotation away from global artificial intelligence stocks. On Monday alone, foreign investors net bought Indian shares valued at 56.73 billion rupees, equivalent to approximately $610.59 million. This strong capital influx helps offset broader regional market corrections.

The anticipated recovery comes despite lingering anxieties over potential US trade tariffs. Reports indicate that the Trump administration is preparing to release the findings of an investigation targeting alleged excess industrial capacity across 16 major trading partners, including India. Broad-based profit-taking had previously caused the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex to fall 1.8 percent on Monday following a four-week winning streak.

Meanwhile, global energy markets continue to ease, providing macroeconomic relief for India. Brent crude futures declined 0.7 percent to $90.8 per barrel amid rising supply and expectations of a market surplus, bringing total price drops for the month of November to approximately 23 percent.

stories.title: Oil prices decline on supply glut concerns and Middle East updates
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices decreased in Tokyo on Wednesday, giving up some of the previous day's gains because rising supply and expectations of a market surplus outweighed worries about Middle East supply disruptions. Brent crude futures dropped 43 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.97 a barrel by 0137 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 47 cents, or 0.6%, to $81.58 a barrel. Both benchmarks had risen over 2% on Tuesday.

Tsuyoshi Ueno, a senior economist at the NLI Research Institute, noted that perceptions of a global supply glut have limited price growth since the International Energy Agency issued a report earlier this month. However, Ueno pointed out that attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and mutual attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have increased uncertainty about this trend. Market attention is also directed toward the upcoming OPEC+ meeting on November 29, where ministers will determine production quotas and output policy for 2027.

According to the International Energy Agency's November 13 statement, the global oil market is projected to return to a surplus in the fourth quarter as Middle East exports recover at a pace faster than worldwide oil demand. Regional supply developments include the reopening of Libya's Sharara oil pipeline after an unlawful group closed a valve, allowing oil to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, as confirmed by the National Oil Corporation chairperson on Monday. Meanwhile, Iraq is urging OPEC+ to increase estimates of its crude oil production capacity, creating tensions during reviews that impact next year's pumping quotas.

Data and industry sources indicate that China and India are on track to record high Russian oil imports this year, filling a supply gap created by the Iran war. In security incidents, Saudi air defences intercepted three Houthi cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh, and a container ship was targeted on an unauthorized route near the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guards. Furthermore, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles while sailing east through the strait on Monday. In inventory news, the American Petroleum Institute reported that US crude stocks increased by 126,000 barrels in the week ending November 20, whereas eight analysts polled by Reuters had estimated an average increase of about 1.5 million barrels.

stories.title: Pakistan expects IMF board to approve $1.21 billion next month
stories.summary:
The Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund is scheduled to decide on December 11 whether to approve the disbursement of approximately $1.21 billion to Pakistan under two active programs. This approval will encompass the fourth review of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility and the third review of the $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility. Upon approval, Pakistan will gain access to about $1 billion under the EFF and roughly $210 million under the RSF, raising the total disbursements across these two arrangements to approximately $5.7 billion. Both the 37-month EFF and the 28-month RSF are set to conclude by September 2027, following a staff-level agreement reached in the first week of October.

During discussions held from September 23 to October 7, an IMF team led by Iva Petrova completed the 2026 Article IV consultation alongside the program reviews. IMF staff recognized that program implementation under the EFF has stayed broadly on track despite a difficult external environment. The Fund commended Pakistan's strong commitment to maintaining macroeconomic stability, strengthening public finances, keeping inflation within the State Bank of Pakistan’s target range, enhancing energy sector viability, and strengthening social protection. Supported by the EFF, authorities successfully navigated the fallout from the Middle East conflict, helping preserve macroeconomic stability while real GDP growth reached 4 percent in the first three quarters of fiscal year 2026.

Although higher energy prices and supply disruptions subsequently softened growth momentum, the IMF estimated full-year GDP growth at 3.6 percent. The current account remained broadly balanced in fiscal year 2026 due to strong remittances, and gross foreign exchange reserves climbed to about $21.5 billion by the end of September. Sovereign credit rating upgrades and renewed access to international financial markets further demonstrated stronger policy credibility. Nevertheless, the IMF underscored notable risks stemming from geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions, and trade disruptions.

To safeguard stability against external shocks, both sides agreed that maintaining sound macroeconomic policies remains essential. Policy priorities will focus on preserving fiscal discipline through the implementation of the fiscal year 2027 budget, which is anchored by an underlying primary surplus of 2 percent of GDP. This strategy is supported by tax policy and revenue administration measures intended to guide public debt onto a sustainable downward trajectory.

stories.title: Pakistan anticipates $1.21 billion IMF disbursement on December 11
stories.summary:
The International Monetary Fund's Executive Board is anticipated to approve approximately $1.21 billion in disbursements for Pakistan on December 11. This decision will mark the completion of the fourth review under the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility and the third review under the $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility. Once approved, Pakistan will receive about $1 billion under the EFF and around $210 million under the RSF, bringing the total disbursements under both arrangements to approximately $5.7 billion. The two concurrent programs, consisting of a 37-month EFF and a 28-month RSF, are scheduled to wrap up by September 2027 following a staff-level agreement reached in early October.

During review discussions conducted from September 23 to October 7, an IMF team led by Iva Petrova also concluded the 2026 Article IV consultation regarding Pakistan's economic performance. IMF staff observed that EFF implementation remained generally on track despite a challenging external setting, highlighting the country's dedication to macroeconomic stability, robust public finances, controlled inflation within the State Bank of Pakistan’s target range, energy sector viability, and social protection. Backed by the EFF, authorities managed the impacts of the Middle East conflict effectively, allowing real GDP growth to hit 4 percent in the first three quarters of fiscal year 2026.

While subsequent supply disruptions and higher energy prices moderated momentum, the IMF estimated full-year growth at 3.6 percent for fiscal year 2026. The current account stayed broadly balanced thanks to strong remittances, and gross foreign exchange reserves reached about $21.5 billion by the end of September. Furthermore, sovereign credit rating upgrades and renewed access to global financial markets reflected enhanced policy credibility. Despite these positive indicators, the Fund warned of significant risks related to geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, global financial tightening, and trade disruptions.

Both parties agreed that continued macroeconomic discipline is vital for protecting stability against external vulnerabilities. Key policy priorities involve maintaining fiscal discipline via the strict execution of the fiscal year 2027 budget, which targets an underlying primary surplus of 2 percent of GDP. These efforts will be backed by tax policy and revenue administration measures designed to ensure a sustainable downward trajectory for public debt.

stories.title: سکھر: ریسکیو ٹیم نے راستہ بھٹکنے والی نایاب بلائنڈ ڈولفن کو دریائے سندھ میں چھوڑ دیا
stories.summary:
سکھر کے قریب راستہ بھٹک کر خیرپور کی علی نواز واہ آر ڈی 100 کے مقام پر پہنچ جانے والی نایاب بلائنڈ ڈولفن کو ریسکیو حکام نے بروقت کارروائی کے بعد دریائے سندھ میں واپس چھوڑ دیا۔ پکا چانگ کے قریب نابینا ڈولفن دیکھے جانے کی اطلاع ملنے پر ریسکیو ٹیم فوری طور پر موقع پر پہنچی تھی۔

ریسکیو کیے جانے کے بعد اس نایاب ڈولفن کو لینس ڈاؤن برج کے مقام پر دریائے سندھ میں منتقل کیا گیا۔ ریسکیو حکام کے فراہم کردہ اعداد و شمار کے مطابق یہ ایک نر ڈولفن ہے جس کی لمبائی تین انچ سے زائد اور وزن 24 اعشاریہ پانچ پانچ کلوگرام ہے۔

ماہرین کے مطابق اس نایاب بلائنڈ ڈولفن کی عمر تین سے ساڑھے تین سال کے درمیان ہے۔ یہ واقعہ اس وقت پیش آیا جب ڈولفن دریائے سندھ میں سفر کرتے ہوئے اپنا راستہ بھٹک گئی تھی اور ایک ذیلی آبی گزرگاہ میں جا نکلی تھی۔

بروقت ریسکیو آپریشن کی بدولت اس نایاب آبی مخلوق کو محفوظ طریقے سے اس کے قدرتی ماحول یعنی دریائے سندھ میں واپس پہنچا دیا گیا۔ اس کامیاب کارروائی پر مقامی سطح پر ریسکیو ٹیم کی پھرتی اور بروقت اقدامات کو سراہا گیا۔

stories.title: Achakzai Urges National Government and Major Reforms at Conference
stories.summary:
Mahmood Khan Achakzai, head of Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan and Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly, called for the establishment of a national government and extensive constitutional reforms during a multi-party conference in Lahore on Tuesday. Speaking at the Javed Iqbal Auditorium of the Lahore High Court Bar Association, Achakzai argued that decisions of national importance must be made through consultations with elected representatives and democratic forces rather than a small group of individuals. He emphasized the necessity of constitutional supremacy, parliamentary sovereignty, and the restoration of democracy.

Achakzai expressed deep concern over deteriorating law and order, noting that unrest and bloodshed previously confined to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan have now spread to Azad Jammu and Kashmir. He stressed that protecting citizens should be the primary duty of the state and highlighted the plight of PTI founder Imran Khan, alleging that authorities are attempting to break his resolve despite a stolen mandate. To address these compounding crises, Achakzai proposed a national government comprising state institutions, political parties, and other stakeholders to correct past injustices, enact reforms, and provide the military with a dignified, constitutional exit from politics.

Other prominent political figures echoed these sentiments during the conference. Senate opposition leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas criticized the current federal approach, questioned the treatment of jailed PTI leaders, and asserted that the existing political system has failed the poor. Hamid Khan, a former president of the Supreme Court Bar Association, also addressed the gathering. This high-profile political assembly matters because it unites opposition leaders in openly challenging federal policies, demanding systemic overhauls, and seeking a fundamental redistribution of political and military power amid mounting national instability.

stories.title: Court Approves Messaging-App Record Access in Mir Raza Murder Case
stories.summary:
A judicial magistrate in Karachi on Tuesday approved an application submitted by the investigating officer in the Mir Ali Raza murder case, granting permission to obtain digital communication records from multiple applications. The request targeted the accounts of the deceased business owner, his business partner Ahmed Bharday, and another individual named Ali Shaz across platforms including WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, iMessage, LinkedIn, and FaceTime. Both Mr. Bharday and Mr. Shaz appeared in court following a formal notice and raised no objections to the request.

During the hearing, the investigating officer, DSP Fareed Ahmed Khan, explained that gathering this digital data is crucial for mapping out communications and activities prior to the fatal incident. He noted that the electronic evidence will help establish the sequence of events, identify contacts, trace potential leads, and corroborate other investigative findings. Although the officer initially approached the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency, he was informed that the data requests required explicit court authorization. Alongside approving the application, the court granted the investigator an additional 14 days to submit the final charge sheet.

The case stems from the tragic death of 25-year-old business owner Mir Raza, who went missing on July 28 after departing from his home in PECHS. His body, which displayed a single gunshot wound, was discovered the following day hidden in bushes within Karachi's Gulistan-i-Jauhar neighborhood. A formal case was subsequently registered at the Ferozabad police station under specific sections of the Pakistan Penal Code related to kidnapping, premeditated murder, and the destruction of evidence.

This judicial decision matters because investigators have struggled for more than three months to identify the actual perpetrator or clarify the full circumstances surrounding the discovery of the victim's body. With a joint investigation team currently reviewing the case under the recommendation of a judicial commission, unlocking digital communications represents a vital step toward breaking the deadlock and securing accountability in a high-profile homicide that has heavily drawn public attention.

stories.title: Internal records reveal compliance challenges for Deutsche Bank in Pakistan
stories.summary:
In 2018, Pakistan was placed on the Financial Action Task Force’s gray list, initiating an urgent national effort to protect its financial system against illicit capital flows. While policymakers scrambled to reinforce financial defenses, internal documents from a massive leak show that vulnerabilities within Deutsche Bank’s Pakistan operations complicated these efforts. Deutsche Bank itself had classified Pakistan as a restricted, high-risk country due to terrorism and Taliban links alongside proximity to Iran, subjecting local businesses to extra checks. However, internal records reviewed by journalists revealed a history of overlooked alerts, bypassed regulations, and challenges in identifying parties moving money within the country.

Deutsche Bank has operated in Pakistan under a commercial banking license since 1962, employing nearly 100 staff across Karachi and Lahore to provide corporate and investment banking services. Despite global compliance issues and billions in fines in other jurisdictions for money laundering failures and interest-rate manipulation, Deutsche Bank's Pakistan branch maintained a clean public reputation. In 2016, Pakistan was a prominent part of the bank's global trade finance business, ranking third behind China and India in letters of credit handled. That year, the bank processed an estimated €872 million in incoming funds and €255 million in outgoing funds for Pakistan, alongside executing hundreds of thousands of cross-border payment instructions.

Local operations relied heavily on manual processes. A December 2019 spreadsheet showed that local teams handled around 4,560 daily items across cash counters, cheque clearing, and electronic payments without full automation, while also conducting over 14,000 daily reviews of transactions flagged by sanctions screening. In October 2019, the State Bank of Pakistan introduced a Trade-Based Money Laundering framework to strengthen anti-money laundering controls, eventually setting a compliance deadline of September 30, 2020.

Internal emails indicate that Deutsche Bank Pakistan missed this deadline by months. On July 30, 2021, principal auditor Khurram Amanullah notified colleagues that the branch had failed to implement a price due diligence mechanism and an automated management information system tool required by the regulator, attributing the delay partly to excessive deliberation over whether to build or outsource the systems. An earlier audit from 2017 similarly noted that the bank's trade finance operations did not always verify whether underlying goods met local requirements or document expected client trade flows.

stories.title: Iranian Currency Plunges on Black Market After Fresh US Sanctions
stories.summary:
Iran's currency experienced a sharp drop on the black market following the announcement of new financial penalties by the United States government. The central bank governor noted that these recent measures targeted a standard platform utilized for registering transactions.

The US Treasury department publicly disclosed restrictions against more than twenty individual exchange houses, front corporations, and people. Officials stated that these entities belonged to a shadow banking system that was supervised directly by the central bank of Iran.

Following the announcement, tracking websites recorded a swift decline in the value of the national currency by Tuesday afternoon. The exchange rate for the US dollar rose to approximately 2.82 million rials, marking an increase of about five percent compared to the previous day's rate of 2.68 million rials.

This currency depreciation highlights ongoing economic pressures in Iran amidst tightening foreign restrictions. Financial monitors continue to observe the declining value of the rial as exchange platforms adapt to the newly imposed US penalties.

stories.title: Pakistan Interior Minister Stresses Four Non-Negotiable Red Lines for Free Speech
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi declared on Tuesday that freedom of speech must not serve as a shield for individuals crossing four specific red lines: terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence, and the sexual exploitation of children. Speaking at an Islamabad seminar titled 'Social Media Platforms and the Post-Truth Era,' organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute, Naqvi criticized social media networks for acting on only 47 percent of complaints filed by the Counter Terrorism Department. He emphasized that while dissent, criticism of the government, and citizen inquiries are acceptable, online platforms are still being utilized by banned outfits like the Baloch Liberation Army to recruit, fundraise, and spread fear.

To address growing cybercrime challenges and institutional limitations within the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency, Naqvi defended the creation of the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority. Both the authority and the agency operate under the amended Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act. Under the new regulatory framework, social media platforms, over-the-top services, and major content creators must register with the authority to ensure accountability. Naqvi clarified that registration is not meant to silence voices and that enforcement will proceed incrementally through engagement, notices, and penalties, with platform blocking reserved as a final measure.

During the event, other speakers also addressed the complexities of digital regulation and rights. Minister for IT and Telecom Shaza Fatima Khawaja emphasized the importance of balancing fundamental freedoms with the protection of citizens' privacy and dignity in the digital age. Senator Azam Nazeer Tarar noted that international jurisdictions like the European Union and the United Kingdom have introduced strict rules to protect women and children from online misinformation. Meanwhile, moderator Syed Talat Hussain highlighted concerns from media professionals and content creators that stringent regulations might grant excessive power to the government.

The matter matters significantly as Pakistan navigates a tense intersection of digital governance, national security, and constitutional rights. With regulatory bodies facing judicial scrutiny and petitions across the country, the debate underscores the state's struggle to contain online radicalization without curtailing legitimate journalistic reporting and public dissent. Representatives from Meta and TikTok also participated, stating that their community guidelines align with Pakistani laws.

stories.title: UN Report Reveals Over 47,000 Women and Girls Killed by Relatives in 2025
stories.summary:
A newly published report from the United Nations reveals that more than 47,000 women and girls were killed globally by intimate partners or family members in 2025. This equates to roughly five female victims every hour, or 129 deaths daily. The figures, released jointly ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women by UN Women and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, indicate that the total number of such homicides has remained virtually unchanged over the past several years, fluctuating between 45,000 and 51,000 annually.

Out of the 78,000 total intentional homicides involving women and girls last year, approximately 60 percent occurred in the private sphere at the hands of family members or partners. While women accounted for 19 percent of global homicide victims overall, the vast majority of female victims were killed domestically, whereas only 11 percent of male homicide victims faced a similar fate. The UN emphasized the critical need for domestic violence prevention strategies to target both intimate relationships and broader family structures.

Geographically, no region was spared from the crisis. Africa recorded the highest absolute toll with 22,100 female victims killed by relatives or partners. Asia followed as the second-highest region with 15,100 victims, while the Americas recorded 7,400, Europe reported 2,100, and Oceania recorded 300 victims. The report also pointed out that although global homicide rates have experienced a general decline, rates of femicide are decreasing at a much slower pace, particularly in the Americas and Europe.

The findings underscore a persistent global crisis regarding domestic violence and female safety. By quantifying the scale of intimate partner and family-perpetrated murders, the UN report highlights the inadequacy of current preventative measures and urges international policymakers to prioritize targeted interventions to protect women and girls within their own homes.

stories.title: Indian Authorities Prevent Cockroach Movement Leader Saurav Das from Traveling to London
stories.summary:
Saurav Das, the 27-year-old chief spokesperson of India's youth-led Cockroach Janata Party, was barred from boarding a flight to London from New Delhi. Das stated that immigration officials at the airport informed him his passport had been flagged, preventing him from attending a series of scheduled speaking engagements at prestigious British universities, including Oxford, Cambridge, the London School of Economics, and Edinburgh. He was specifically scheduled to address the Oxford Union society on December 1 regarding the viral youth movement's protests.

Das criticized the action on social media, accusing the government of being anti-intellectual and fearful of his message reaching academic institutions abroad. The travel restriction follows a prior detention a month earlier, when Das was detained for defying a security crackdown in New Delhi during demonstrations that demanded the resignation of India's chief election commissioner. The Cockroach Janata Party has rapidly amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May, drawing national attention through youth mobilization.

The movement gained significant political leverage in July when protests organized over alleged examination irregularities successfully forced the education minister to resign. This rare climbdown by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration marked a notable political victory for the group. Critics contend that under Modi's leadership, which began in 2014, India has witnessed a steady decline in both press freedom and human rights.

The incident matters as it highlights the ongoing tensions between youth political activism and state authorities in India. By stopping a prominent opposition figure from engaging with international academic forums, the episode draws further scrutiny to how the government manages dissent, freedom of movement, and political opposition from emerging youth movements.

stories.title: Pakistan Warns of Global Energy and Food Crises Driven by Escalating Conflicts
stories.summary:
Pakistan has warned the United Nations Security Council that widening international conflicts are severely disrupting global food and energy supply chains, pushing up commodity prices, and posing disproportionate economic risks to developing nations. Speaking at a high-level UN briefing in Washington on November 24, 2026, Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, called for the urgent protection of critical energy infrastructure, maritime routes, and agricultural trade networks.

Highlighting the wider ripple effects of geopolitical instability, Shah noted that humanitarian and economic fallout extends far beyond direct conflict zones. Pakistan remains particularly vulnerable to such disruptions due to its heavy reliance on imported oil and gas. According to the International Monetary Fund, Pakistan is a net energy importer with 81 percent of its fuel supplies sourced from Gulf Cooperation Council countries. International conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, have historically strained these supply lines, forcing the country to contemplate expensive spot-market liquefied natural gas purchases—trading between $20 and $30 per million British thermal units according to Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik—and driving up domestic inflation, which averaged 10.2 percent between March and June 2026.

The Security Council briefing, chaired by Latvian President Edgars Rinkvis, specifically addressed the maintenance of peace and security and the protection of critical infrastructure. Shah expressed deep concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure, transportation networks, and commercial vessels. He urged all warring parties to respect international humanitarian law, facilitate unhindered humanitarian assistance, and safeguard interconnected sectors like fertilizers and maritime transport to prevent widespread food insecurity.

Emphasizing that infrastructural safeguards alone cannot solve the underlying instability, Shah concluded that lasting solutions require the peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with the UN Charter and international law. The session also featured remarks from UN Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo, World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg, and UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo.

stories.title: US Army Prepares to Detonate Degraded Lead Azide in Iowa
stories.summary:
The US army instructed residents in a small Iowa community to prepare for a potential evacuation on Wednesday ahead of a planned controlled detonation of nearly 10,000 pounds, or 4,500 kilograms, of degraded lead azide. Lead azide is an explosive chemical historically utilized to ignite military munitions. Although the military eventually moved away from utilizing the substance, various installations around the country sent stockpiles to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown in 2009 for storage and continuous monitoring.

During a press conference, officials outlined several mitigation measures implemented recently. These safety precautions featured earthworks built around two concrete magazines covered in earth that currently house the chemical, misting systems designed to dampen the surrounding terrain, and special foam intended to capture particulates released during the blast. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle stated that the explosion at the Middletown facility was scheduled for 1500 GMT on Wednesday, citing weather forecasts deemed ideal for safeguarding public health and safety throughout the region.

The US Federal Emergency Management Agency issued an alert on Tuesday indicating that individuals located within eight kilometers of the blast might face evacuation orders. Meanwhile, people living between eight and 30 kilometers away were instructed to stay indoors with their windows shut to prevent exposure to lead dust. New maps published by the army project that dust could settle on surfaces as far as 60 kilometers away from the center of the explosion, following a narrow path stretching southwest through southeastern Iowa and into northern Missouri.

Airborne particles are expected to travel significantly further, potentially reaching nearly 150 kilometers away eight hours after the detonation occurs. The army announced plans to issue updated projection maps utilizing hourly weather forecasts starting six hours prior to the explosion, alongside a final estimate following the event. Military officials have been working to identify the safest method to destroy the volatile substance since March, when they discovered degradation that could trigger a spontaneous explosion.

stories.title: China Launches Shenzhou-24 Mission Featuring First Pakistani Astronaut
stories.summary:
China successfully launched the Shenzhou-24 space flight on Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Propelled by a Long March-2F rocket at 8:18 a.m., the spacecraft carried a three-man crew to the Tiangong space station to advance international cooperation in orbit.

The mission features 40-year-old Zeeshan Ali, who becomes the first Pakistani national to travel into space. Serving as a payload specialist, Ali is scheduled to stay at the station for five to ten days to conduct various experiments. His crewmates include Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi.

Prior to the launch, Ali underwent a seven-month training program in Beijing that included intensive Chinese-language classes, learning songs, reading poetry, and practicing table tennis. Beijing has increasingly promoted the Tiangong station as an international hub, particularly as the NASA-led International Space Station faces potential retirement by 2030.

Expressing gratitude to the Chinese government, Ali noted before the flight that he carries the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis on his shoulders. The historic mission highlights expanding space cooperation between China and Pakistan.

stories.title: Zeeshan Ali Enters Orbit as First Pakistani Astronaut on Shenzhou-24
stories.summary:
Zeeshan Ali made history on Wednesday by becoming the first Pakistani astronaut to enter orbit aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft. The mission lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 8:18am Beijing Time using a Long March-2F rocket, successfully reaching its preset orbit shortly after launch.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal witnessed the departure in China and hailed the event as a monumental step for Pakistan's space program. Once docked with the Tiangong space station, Ali will also break ground as the first foreign national to board the Chinese facility. He joins mission commander Tang Hongbo and pilot Wu Yi for a week-long stay involving scientific experiments.

The China Manned Space Agency stated that the crew will perform approximately 90 experiments during the mission. These objectives include orbital rotation with the previous Shenzhou-23 crew, routine space station maintenance, and payload research. Meanwhile, departing Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu will remain on board for an extended period to study human bodily adaptation in space.

Ali was selected following a cooperation agreement signed in February 2025 between Pakistan's space agency Suparco and the China Manned Space Agency. Speaking before the flight, Ali expressed deep gratitude, emphasizing that his journey serves as a launch pad for future joint space exploration between the two nations.

stories.title: Pakistan Sends Its First Astronaut to China's Tiangong Station
stories.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has received a formal send-off as Pakistan's first astronaut, preparing for a historic flight aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft. The mission lifts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China at 5:18am Pakistan time. Ali joins Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi as a payload specialist for a roughly one-week stay at the Tiangong space station.

During his time in orbit, Ali will perform scheduled scientific research and install experimental equipment. The work builds upon four biotechnology experiments selected from over 300 proposals submitted to the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) by universities across Pakistan. These studies target areas including food security and climate change.

The flight stems from an agreement signed between Pakistan and China in February 2025 to select and train Pakistani astronauts. Following three screening rounds, Ali and Khurram Dawood were chosen as candidates, with Dawood serving as the backup. This journey marks the first time a foreign astronaut visits China's space station and the first joint crewed flight involving foreign and Chinese crew members.

Leaders including President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have congratulated the nation on the milestone. Zardari hailed it as a landmark achievement and a source of national pride, while Sharif thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping and paid tribute to SUPARCO, scientists, and the armed forces for their contributions to the historic flight.

stories.title: Czech Republic Defeats Canada to Advance to Davis Cup Semi-Finals
stories.summary:
The Czech Republic kicked off the Davis Cup finals in Bologna, Italy, on November 24, 2026, by defeating Canada 2-0 to claim a spot in the semi-finals. Tomas Machac and Jiri Lehecka secured the victories in the opening singles matches against Liam Draxl and Felix Auger-Aliassime, respectively, giving the two-time former winners an unassailable lead ahead of the doubles matches.

World number 59 Machac earned the first point for the Czech squad by overcoming 154th-ranked Liam Draxl with a score of 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 at the Super Tennis Arena. Following that encounter, top-seeded Jiri Lehecka, ranked 14th in the world, faced former world number four Felix Auger-Aliassime in a high-intensity matchup. After a tightly contested first set that went to a tie-break won by Lehecka, the Czech player broke his opponent's serve in the second set to seal a 7-6(7/4), 6-2 triumph.

Reflecting on the atmosphere, Machac noted the unique challenge posed by the passionate crowd compared to standard tournaments. With the victory secured, the Czech Republic advances to the last four, where they will compete against either three-time defending champions Italy or South Korea.

This crucial win moves the Czech team one step closer to the tournament title as the long tennis season reaches its climax. The event in Bologna continues to draw significant attention as the remaining nations battle for the prestigious team trophy.

stories.title: Zeeshan Ali Becomes Pakistan's First Astronaut to Reach Orbit
stories.summary:
Forty-year-old pilot Zeeshan Ali is set to become Pakistan's first astronaut in orbit as a payload specialist on China's Shenzhou-24 space mission. The spacecraft is scheduled to launch aboard a Long March-2F rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China, heading toward China's Tiangong space station.

Ali joins a three-member crew commanded by China's Tang Hongbo, with Wu Yi serving as the mission pilot. Upon docking with the Tiangong space station, Ali will also become the first foreign national to board the facility. During his roughly one-week stay in space, Ali will participate in conducting approximately 90 experiments alongside the Chinese crew, contributing to ongoing space science research and routine maintenance operations.

Selected from Pakistan alongside Khurram Daud in April following a cooperation agreement signed between Suparco and the China Manned Space Agency in February 2025, Ali expressed deep gratitude to the Chinese government. Speaking at a press briefing in Jiayuguan, he emphasized that he carried the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis and viewed the mission as a launch pad for future bilateral space cooperation.

The Tiangong space station, fully operational since late 2022, can host up to six astronauts during crew handovers. Ali's historic flight marks a significant milestone in Pakistan's space history and opens new avenues for future joint space exploration initiatives between Pakistan and China.

stories.title: Jennifer Barreto of Puerto Rico Crowned Miss Universe 2026 in San Juan
stories.summary:
Jennifer Barreto representing Puerto Rico won the title of Miss Universe 2026 at the seventy-fifth annual competition held in San Juan. The twenty-seven-year-old secured her victory in front of an enthusiastic home crowd on Tuesday night, receiving the crown from the previous year's winner, Fátima Bosch of Mexico.

Barreto competed against 115 international participants throughout the event. The program started the preceding week featuring private interviews alongside a national costume showcase, followed by preliminary swimsuit and evening gown rounds.
