The government of Pakistan has finalized a comprehensive framework to break down the country's two major gas monopolies, Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL), into six to eight separate entities. Submitted to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for clearance, the plan aims to establish a competitive gas market by legally and operationally separating gas transmission and distribution from supply and marketing activities. Technical support for the restructuring was provided by the World Bank, KPMG, and Wood Mackenzie, with the International Monetary Fund also supporting the reforms.

The reform plan proposes creating at least four gas sales entities, divided into two competitive gas supply companies for commercial and industrial users and two regulated entities for domestic consumers. To foster competition, the Sui companies will be required to free up twenty percent of their supply portfolios for private participants in the first year, and ten percent in each of the subsequent two years. Financial projections indicate that while transportation and commercial segments will be profitable, the residential segment will incur losses due to heavily subsidized tariffs. Consequently, the government plans to gradually raise domestic gas prices, reduce billing slabs, and introduce direct subsidies for vulnerable households through a social safety net.

Additionally, over three trillion rupees in gas circular debt will be shifted to a special purpose vehicle funded by a consumer tariff surcharge. The restructuring also outlines massive capital expenditure requirements, including seven hundred thirty-six billion rupees for SNGPL and three hundred ninety billion rupees for SSGCL over several years to upgrade infrastructure and reduce system losses. Transaction advisers will be engaged to help implement the transition over the next five to six months, with the full rollout targeted for the fourth quarter of 2027.

This unbundling initiative matters because it addresses deep-seated financial distortions and structural inefficiencies within Pakistan's energy sector. By dismantling traditional monopolies and introducing market competition, the reforms seek to achieve long-term energy security, price rationality, and an investment-friendly economy while meeting critical international lending conditionalities.

stories.title: چنگیز خان کی زندگی، فتوحات اور دریائے سندھ کے کنارے جلال الدین سے جنگ
stories.summary:
تقریباً آٹھ سو سال پہلے تیموجن نامی منگول خانہ بدوش نے بحیرہ اسود سے بحرالکاہل تک ایک وسیع سلطنت قائم کی جو بعد میں چنگیز خان کے نام سے مشہور ہوا۔ ابتدائی زندگی غربت اور مشکلات میں گزارنے کے بعد اس نے چین، وسطی ایشیا، ایران، روس اور مشرقی یورپ کے حصوں پر حکومت قائم کی۔ مورخین کے مطابق اس کی سلطنت بارہ ملین مربع میل پر پھیلی ہوئی تھی۔

چنگیز خان نے کم عمر میں ہی اپنے سوتیلے بھائی کو قتل کر دیا تھا اور وہ اپنی عسکری حکمت عملی اور نفسیاتی مہارت کے لیے جانا جاتا تھا۔ اس نے اپنی زندگی خیموں اور میدانِ جنگ میں گزاری۔ فارسی مؤرخ منہاج السراج جوزجانی اور دیگر مورخین کے مطابق چنگیز خان ایک بے رحم اور ظالم حکمران تھا جو غداروں کو سخت سزائیں دیتا تھا، تاہم وہ اپنے نواسوں سے بہت پیار کرتا تھا اور بعض مواقع پر اس نے نرمی کا مظاہرہ بھی کیا۔

سنہ 1211 سے 1216 کے دوران چین کو فتح کرنے کے بعد وہ جلال الدین کا تعاقب کرتے ہوئے ہندوستان کی سرحد تک جا پہنچا۔ چنگیز خان اور جلال الدین کی افواج کے درمیان آخری معرکہ 24 نومبر کو دریائے سندھ کے کنارے ہوا۔ منگولوں کے گھیرے میں آنے پر جلال الدین نے اپنے گھوڑے سمیت 180 فٹ گہرے دریا میں چھلانگ لگا دی اور دوسرے کنارے پر پہنچ گیا۔

جلال الدین کی اس دلیری کو دیکھ کر چنگیز خان نے اسے نشانہ نہ بنانے کا حکم دیا، تاہم جلال کے اکثر سپاہی اور تمام بیٹے مارے گئے۔ جلال الدین وہاں سے دہلی گیا جہاں سلطان التمش نے اسے پناہ دینے سے انکار کر دیا، لیکن وہ ہندوستان میں ہی رہا یہاں تک کہ چنگیز خان نے اس کا پیچھا کرنے کا خیال ترک کر دیا۔

stories.title: قطری وزیراعظم اور امریکی وزیر خارجہ کی ملاقات سمیت پاکستان کی اہم خبراں
stories.summary:
قطر کے وزیراعظم محمد بن عبدالرحمان سے امریکی وزیر خارجہ مارکو روبیو نے ملاقات کی جس میں دوطرفہ تعلقات اور ڈائیلاگ کو آگے بڑھانے پر تبادلہ خیال کیا گیا۔ اس موقع پر قطری وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ نئے شعبوں میں تعاون کا مقصد دونوں ممالک کے مفادات اور امنگوں کو پورا کرنا ہے۔ اس اجلاس میں جوہری تحفظ کے نئے چیلنجز اور عالمی تعاون کے فروغ پر بھی بات چیت کی گئی۔

پاکستان کے حوالے سے مختلف خبروں میں بتایا گیا کہ پرتگالی وزیر خارجہ نے صدر مملکت آصف علی زرداری سے ملاقات کی، جس دوران صدر زرداری نے تجارت اور سرمایہ کاری کے لیے مشترکہ ورکنگ گروپ کے قیام کی تجویز دی۔ سندھ ہائی کورٹ نے نیب ترامیم کے بعد 50 کروڑ سے کم مالیت کے مقدمات سے متعلق 27 اپیلیں مسترد کر دیں۔ آئی جی سندھ جاوید عالم اوڈھو نے کراچی میں کاروکاری کے واقعات کو تشویشناک قرار دیا۔

پنجاب کی سطح پر وزیراعلیٰ مریم نواز نے صوبے میں پہلی مرتبہ جھینگوں کے جدید اور مربوط فارم ہاؤسز قائم کرنے کا اعلان کیا۔ مظفرگڑھ کے علاقے سیت پور میں ایک شخص نے تیز دھار آلے سے اپنی دو بیٹیوں کو قتل کرنے کے بعد خود کو اور بیوی کو زخمی کر دیا۔ حکومت کی جانب سے اگلے چوبیس گھنٹوں کے لیے پیٹرول سستا اور ڈیزل کی قیمت برقرار رکھنے کا نوٹیفیکیشن جاری کیا گیا۔

دیگر خبروں میں نیشنل سائبر کرائم انویسٹی گیشن ایجنسی نے لاہور سے سائبر ہراسانی اور بھتا خوری میں ملوث ملزم کو گرفتار کیا۔ اسلام آباد کی عدالت نے فاطمہ اصغر ہلاکت کیس میں کم عمر بچوں سے ملازمت کے قانون کی دفعہ لگانے کا حکم دیا۔ الیکشن کمیشن نے عائشہ گلالئی کی جماعت صفا کی چیئرپرسن ہونے کا نوٹیفیکیشن جاری کر دیا۔

stories.title: Pakistani Astronaut Zeeshan Ali Assigned to China’s Shenzhou-24 Space Mission
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s astronaut Mohammad Zeeshan Ali has been selected to join China’s upcoming Shenzhou-24 crewed space mission, which is scheduled to lift off on November 25. The announcement was made by the China Manned Space Agency. Zeeshan will serve as a payload specialist during the orbital mission and will return aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked with the Tiangong space station in May. The crewed spaceship is set to launch at 8:18 am Beijing Time from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi on a three-member mission.

During his expected one-week stay in space, Zeeshan will participate in conducting approximately 90 different experiments alongside the Chinese crew. His selection follows an agreement signed in February 2025 between Suparco and the China Manned Space Agency, which outlined training for two Pakistani astronauts in China. In April, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Zeeshan and fellow astronaut Khurram Daud after they were chosen for training, praising the milestone as a source of national pride that enhances bilateral ties.

The collaboration highlights close relations between Beijing and Islamabad, as China serves as Pakistan's largest trading partner and a major foreign investor. China has significantly advanced its space program in recent years, aiming to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030. Since being barred from the International Space Station in 2011 due to US legislative restrictions prohibiting NASA from collaborating with Chinese agencies, Beijing has increasingly built international partnerships, such as the cooperative agreement with Pakistan.

stories.title: Rawalpindi Police Submit Investigation Challan in Hina Javed Murder Case
stories.summary:
Police in Rawalpindi have officially submitted the challan for the murder case of 45-year-old Hina Javed to the District Prosecution Branch. The submission follows the completion of the investigation and the inclusion of forensic reports into the official case record. The district prosecutor has received the paperwork and initiated a formal scrutiny process.

Sources revealed that the initial investigation found no incriminating evidence against the victim's husband. Consequently, his name was placed in Column No II of the challan, leaving any further decisions regarding his status to the discretion of the court. The prosecution branch noted that if any legal deficiencies are identified during the review, the file may be returned to the police for rectification before being presented to the court of the district and sessions judge.

Hina Javed was murdered at her residence on August 20, leading to a murder case registered at the Civil Lines police station. The investigation has faced public scrutiny, as the victim's family previously expressed a lack of confidence in how police handled the inquiry. Civil society members have also held vigils to mourn her death.

The case has drawn significant public attention amidst various local reports concerning crime, safety perception indices, and judicial proceedings. The ongoing scrutiny remains a critical step before the matter is formally heard in the sessions court.

stories.title: Israeli Strikes in Gaza Kill UNRWA Worker and Two Others
stories.summary:
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza have resulted in the deaths of at least three people, including an employee of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees (UNRWA). Medics and agency officials identified the slain UNRWA worker as Adel Al-Helo, who was killed near a water well in the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza while performing his regular duties.

According to an UNRWA spokesperson, Al-Helo was working alongside staff and a guard to supply water to local residents when the area was struck, leaving three others wounded. Al-Helo had served the agency for 35 years. Later on Monday, a separate airstrike targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, killing two additional people and wounding others. These incidents occur despite a US-backed ceasefire brokered in October 2025, which halted major fighting but failed to stop ongoing Israeli attacks or secure Hamas's disarmament.

In a separate political development, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz announced a plan to transfer civilian criminal enforcement regarding Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank from the military to the Israel Police. Katz stated that the Israel Defense Forces should not handle civilian law enforcement over the Jewish population, following recent incidents of settlers torching Palestinian vehicles and properties. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's caretaker government is evaluating the measure, which critics suggest could be a step toward annexation.

The prolonged conflict has caused severe humanitarian crises, widespread displacement, and international scrutiny. Israeli authorities have stated they are investigating the recent settler violence, while leaders such as President Isaac Herzog have condemned extremist actions.

stories.title: Iran Vows to Counter US Naval Blockade and Seeks $290 Billion
stories.summary:
Iran announced on Monday that it will use all available means to counter a naval blockade imposed by the United States. During a weekly briefing, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei characterized the blockade of Iranian ports—enacted by Washington in response to Iran's efforts to close the Strait of Hormuz—as an act of military aggression. Citing Article 51 of the UN Charter, Baqaei asserted that Tehran is entitled to defend itself using any necessary means.

Simultaneously, Iranian judicial authorities announced that domestic courts have ordered Washington to pay $290 billion in damages over decades of hostility. Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary’s centre for lawyers, stated that lawsuits have also been filed against Gulf Arab nations for allowing their territories to be used for attacks against Iran. The current escalation follows strikes on February 28 that resulted in the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, prompting regional retaliations by Iranian forces against US-Israeli assets.

Despite the tensions, Tehran indicated a conditional willingness to de-escalate. Baqaei stated that security and normal transit through the Strait of Hormuz could be restored within two days if the American side fulfills its commitments, which includes lifting the naval blockade.

The ongoing maritime standoff has disrupted global energy supplies and put diplomatic ceasefires to the test. Washington has implemented economic sanctions and established a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran, while Tehran maintains its hardline stance against the naval restrictions.

stories.title: Kurdish Fighters Evacuate Fourteen Bases in Northern Iraq
stories.summary:
Kurdish fighters have pulled out from 14 additional bases located in northern Iraq, according to state media reports citing Turkish intelligence services on Monday. This military reduction serves as a vital component of a developing peace agreement between the Kurdistan Workers’ Party and Ankara, which is designed to halt decades of conflict that has caused at least 50,000 fatalities.

The strategic evacuations occurred on November 18 within the Hakurk region, a mountainous area bordering Iraq, Turkiye, and Iran that has historically served as a primary rear base for the fighters. State news agency Anadolu, referencing Turkish MIT intelligence sources, stated that these shelters and caves were rendered unusable during the departure. Security sources noted that every positive development moves them closer to reintegrating individuals under legal frameworks.

This follows an announcement from the PKK last month confirming their withdrawal from four other key bases in northern Iraq, a move also verified by Turkish intelligence. The actions succeed a legislative bill passed by Turkiye two months prior offering limited amnesty to PKK militants as part of a two-year peace initiative. Turkish authorities maintain that the total disarmament and dissolution of the group must be formally confirmed by the National Security Council and published in the official government journal.

The broader dissolution process is currently being managed by a Coordination Board consisting of four specialized sub-committees. While officials anticipate the National Security Council to convene soon, concrete and verifiable developments on the ground indicate that the overall peace process is progressing in the correct direction.

stories.title: Former Prince Andrew Accused of Accepting Bribe for Turkish Heiress
stories.summary:
Britain's former prince Andrew allegedly accepted a payment of $976,000 as a bribe to assist a Turkish heiress, the High Court in London was informed on Monday. The disgraced royal, now officially known as Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, is scheduled to provide testimony during the ongoing civil trial on December 14 after being compelled by a witness summons.

The high-stakes litigation involves Nebahat Isbilen, whose family established the Evyap soap and cosmetics group, suing her former business adviser Selman Turk. Isbilen alleges that Turk misappropriated tens of millions of pounds without explanation, a claim he denies. According to legal submissions, Isbilen previously wrote to Andrew at the outset of the proceedings, prompting him to return the funds, though he faces no formal accusations of wrongdoing in the matter.

The legal dispute highlights financial dealings involving Andrew and his ex-wife, Sarah Ferguson. Isbilen's filings state that Turk transferred approximately two million pounds to a firm called Alphabet Capital, with portions reaching the former Duke and Duchess of York. Isbilen sought Turk's assistance to relocate her fortune out of Turkiye following her husband's imprisonment in 2015 on politically motivated charges, and claims Turk deceived her regarding the payment to Andrew.

Conversely, legal representatives for Turk argued that Isbilen understood the transaction to be a bribe intended to secure assistance regarding her passport, UK residency, or her husband's legal case. Turk's lawyer stated that the payment was recorded at the bank as a gift made with the expectation that the former prince would intervene on her behalf.

stories.title: Houthi Officials Report Seventeen Deaths from Coalition Air Strikes in Yemen
stories.summary:
Yemeni Houthi authorities reported that Saudi-led coalition air strikes targeting telecommunications facilities in the Red Sea governorate of Hodeida resulted in seventeen deaths and eleven injuries. The Monday attacks caused total destruction of administrative buildings, a mosque, and staff housing, while severely disrupting internet and telecommunications services for tens of thousands of residents. In a separate incident, a Houthi military spokesman stated that coalition strikes also hit buses and transport vehicles in the southwestern governorate of Lahj, causing further casualties. Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on these reported strikes, and the claims remain independently unverified.

The escalation follows a series of recent cross-border military actions, including a reported ballistic missile interception by the coalition off Saudi Arabia's western Red Sea coast and a claimed Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery. The conflict in Yemen, which has endured more than a decade of civil war, intensified significantly after a truce collapsed in July, resulting in over sixteen hundred deaths and more than three hundred thousand displaced persons according to United Nations figures.

Despite ongoing regional instability and maritime incidents near the Strait of Hormuz, global crude oil prices declined following reports of increased Middle East supplies and the restoration of Libya's Sharara oil pipeline. Brent crude futures fell to eighty-nine dollars and thirty-two cents a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate dropped to eighty dollars and forty-four cents. However, market analysts emphasized that geopolitical tensions and security risks for shipping lanes remain acute.

These developments highlight the fragile security landscape of the region, where persistent military confrontations between the Houthi movement and the Saudi-led coalition continue to cause civilian casualties, disrupt vital infrastructure, and threaten international energy markets amid broader geopolitical conflicts.

stories.title: Islamabad Hosts Annual International Meeting on Global Nuclear Security Training
stories.summary:
Pakistan formally opened the 2026 annual meeting of the International Network for Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres in Islamabad, welcoming sixty-eight delegates from forty-nine countries. Hosted at the Pakistan Centre of Excellence for Nuclear Security in collaboration with the International Atomic Energy Agency, the four-day conference brings together global policymakers, regulators, and technical experts to share best practices and address emerging nuclear security challenges. This marks the network's return to the Pakistani capital a decade after it hosted the milestone 2016 gathering, which was the first annual meeting held outside IAEA headquarters in Vienna.

In a video address, IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi praised Pakistan for hosting the event and highlighted the network's vital role in translating nuclear security theory into effective practice. As an increasing number of nations adopt nuclear applications for electricity, medicine, and agriculture, Grossi emphasized that international cooperation and shared expertise are more critical than ever. Delivering the keynote speech, Additional Foreign Secretary Ambassador Khalil Hussain Hashmi reaffirmed Pakistan's long-standing partnership with the UN nuclear watchdog and underscored the necessity of strong national institutions and skilled professionals in maintaining robust security frameworks.

The opening session was inaugurated by Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority Chairman Zia Hussain Shah, who stressed the importance of continuous investment in specialized human resource development. Following the inaugural events, participating diplomats and IAEA representatives toured advanced laboratories at the Centre of Excellence for Nuclear Security. The conference schedule includes technical working group sessions and visits to the National Institute of Safety and Security and the Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences to foster deeper international technical exchanges through Thursday.

Hosting this prominent international gathering underscores Pakistan's active participation in global nuclear security governance and its commitment to collaborative capacity building. The event provides a crucial platform for nations to strengthen professional competencies, secure nuclear materials, and support the safe expansion of peaceful nuclear technologies worldwide.

stories.title: Opposition Walkout in Balochistan Assembly Over Fazlur Rehman Security Withdrawal
stories.summary:
Opposition legislators in the Balochistan Assembly organized a walkout on Monday to protest the removal of security guards assigned to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman. Lawmakers later returned to the chamber following mediation and appeals from provincial ministers.

The assembly meeting was overseen by Dr Ashok Kumar from the Panel of Chairmen. Immediately following the commencement, JUI-F MPA Zahid Reki raised a point of order regarding the security withdrawal, emphasizing that the Maulana had already survived two separate assassination attempts. Reki condemned the decision and cautioned that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would face accountability if any harm befell his party leader before walking out. National Party chief Dr Abdul Malik Baloch also voiced concern over the situation, announcing a sympathetic walkout by his party members.

In response, Home Minister Ziaullah Langove stated he lacked specific details concerning the security reduction but praised the JUI-F chief as a seasoned politician. Langove emphasized that the nation faces a critical period and warned that making critical statements against security institutions performing sacrifices was inappropriate. Provincial Minister Noor Muhammad Dummar echoed these sentiments regarding the armed forces.

Following successful intervention by provincial ministers, the protesting opposition members ended their boycott and returned to the session. Concluding the assembly business, the house passed both the Balochistan Fisheries and Aquaculture Bill and the Balochistan Non-Formal Education Bill before adjourning until December 8.

stories.title: Senate Body Discloses Punjab Holds Over Sixty Percent of Senior Federal Posts
stories.summary:
A Senate subcommittee in Islamabad revealed that Punjab holds over sixty percent of senior administrative positions in the Federal Secretariat, sparking strong criticism from lawmakers. During a meeting chaired by Senator Barrister Zamir Hussain Ghumro, the Establishment Division presented domicile-based employment data for Basic Pay Scales eighteen through twenty-two for the twenty twenty-five to twenty twenty-six period. The committee determined that Punjab's representation at sixty point one seven percent violates Article thirty-eight clause g of the Constitution, which mandates the strict enforcement of equitable provincial quotas in federal services and statutory bodies. Lawmakers demanded immediate rectification to ensure fair representation for smaller provinces, particularly Sindh and Balochistan.

The subcommittee also criticized the persistence of a rural-urban divide in Sindh, declaring it contrary to constitutional provisions, and expressed dissatisfaction with the Establishment Division's failure to submit a comprehensive rectification plan. Lawmakers directed officials to eliminate the rural-urban split for Sindh, ensure transparency in recruitment without nepotism, and submit detailed corrective plans within two weeks. Additionally, the Establishment Division was asked to provide vacancy details from the Federal Public Service Commission while highlighting recent efforts to advertise over five thousand posts for Balochistan and facilitate local applicants.

In the same session, the subcommittee reviewed the petroleum ministry's compliance with Article one hundred seventy-two clause three of the Constitution, which guarantees joint and equal ownership of oil and natural gas resources between the federal government and respective provinces. Senator Ghumro pointed out that sixteen years after the eighteenth constitutional amendment, profits earned by four major petroleum companies alone exceeded three point six trillion rupees, with not a single penny distributed to the provinces. Total provincial losses may surpass six trillion rupees when other corporations are included.

The committee directed the petroleum ministry to urgently formulate a formal mechanism for sharing oil and gas profits equally with provincial governments and submit it to the federal cabinet. This oversight matters because it addresses persistent constitutional grievances regarding provincial employment quotas and resource revenue sharing, ensuring that marginalized regions receive their lawful financial and administrative entitlements.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Large-Scale Manufacturing Growth Remains Modest Amid Sector Disparities
stories.summary:
Large-scale manufacturing growth in Pakistan remains modest, with cumulative growth for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 clocking in at 2.07 percent, falling below the performance of the corresponding period last year. Following four quarters of stronger expansion leading up to the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 and two subsequent quarters of subdued activity, the industrial recovery has moderated rather than stalled. However, the latest growth has become heavily dependent on a single sector, with wearing apparel driving the trend.

Ready-made garment export quantities account for more than half of the positive contribution to large-scale manufacturing growth, surging 17 percent year-on-year during the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 and continuing upward through October. Automobiles represent the second-largest positive contributor, though this recovery is measured against an exceptionally weak production base caused by a demand collapse between 2023 and 2025. Petroleum products rank third, bolstered by higher refinery utilization and attractive margins amid Middle East conflict, while motor gasoline output remained close to all-time highs in September.

Conversely, widespread weakness persists across other industries, with ten sectors currently in negative territory according to the diffusion index—the highest count since August 2025. Food manufacturing was the largest drag in September, with ghee and vegetable oil production dropping to multi-year lows, though an anticipated larger sugarcane crop may help revive the sector. Meanwhile, chemicals and pharmaceuticals continue to face pressure from supply disruptions, procurement difficulties, and high raw material costs that offset the benefits of cheaper electricity.

Overall, the industrial outlook continues to reflect moderate growth constrained by subdued household purchasing power, elevated input costs, and uncertain demand. While garment exports, recovering automobile manufacturing, and active refineries provide key support, broader economic recovery depends on domestic demand catching up with macroeconomic stabilization. Interest rates are not expected to decline rapidly, which may further delay recovery in interest-sensitive sectors throughout the first half of the fiscal year.
